later.text: WAR 61 3.1.4 and 5.5: the hamlet at Schuitevoerderslaan, late 8th and early 9th century, a house of 6 by 20 m, perhaps two field ovens, given up before 900.

pages.title: The eel stakes
pages.hint: A fishery, not yet seen
pages.brief: A fishery at Medemelacha. Where the stream runs out into the lake of Wervershoof: lines of stakes and wicker eel traps in the reeds, a punt pulled up, no house in sight and the king's ground hidden round the bend.
pages.game: A fishery at Medemelacha. Where the stream runs out into the lake of Wervershoof: lines of stakes and wicker eel traps in the reeds, a punt pulled up, no house in sight and the king's ground hidden round the bend. By day herons. By night, now and then, two boats lying side by side without a light and the sound of something heavy being handed across. What is done here: buy from makers, use your store and wait for wind. Found here: Eilbern.

pages.title: The trees on the ridge
pages.hint: A holy wood, not yet seen
pages.brief: A holy wood at Medemelacha. The only trees for a day's walk: alder, birch and a few old oaks on the sand, west of the last house.
pages.game: A holy wood at Medemelacha. The only trees for a day's walk: alder, birch and a few old oaks on the sand, west of the last house. Under the biggest oak the grass is trodden, and there are things in the fork of it that nobody put there by accident: a cheese rind, a twist of wool, a cow's horn. Elk tracks cross the wet ground behind. What is done here: make an offering, cast the lots and have him remembered.
pages.known: Archeologie in West-Friesland 13: trees on the ridge, open moss beyond; WAR 61 2.3.2: the country round was still largely heathen in Carolingian times; elk bone of about 700 (WAR 61 4.10.2.8). The offering tree is invented (?).

pages.title: The Frisians' shore
pages.hint: A landing, not yet seen
pages.brief: A landing at Mogontia. In front, a gravel bank with river boats nosed onto it and short plank jetties running out from long narrow plots.
pages.game: A landing at Mogontia. In front, a gravel bank with river boats nosed onto it and short plank jetties running out from long narrow plots. Behind, timber houses gable-on to the water, and behind them the grey Roman wall, taller than any roof. Tow ropes dry on rails; it smells of wet hemp, wine lees and pitch, and Frisian is spoken louder than Frankish. What is done here: load and unload, hire carriers, ask the keeper, wait for wind and buy a plot. Found here: Folcbald.
pages.known: Landesmuseum Mainz, Aurea Magontia, 'From near and far': long plots from the wall to the river with jetties, Frisian traders settled there.

later.text: Annales Fuldenses 886.
Certain in 886, likely earlier, undated for 793.

pages.title: The river gate, Mogontia
pages.hint: A toll place, not yet seen
pages.brief: A toll place at Mogontia. A Roman gate arch in the wall above the shore, its stone worn hollow by cart wheels, with a lean-to of planks against it where the bishop's man sits with a tally stick.
pages.game: A toll place at Mogontia. A Roman gate arch in the wall above the shore, its stone worn hollow by cart wheels, with a lean-to of planks against it where the bishop's man sits with a tally stick. Through the arch, a strip of street and then cabbages. Carts of casks wait in a line; a mule complains. What is done here: pay the toll, show the charter and hear the law.
pages.known: The Roman wall: de.wikipedia 'Mainzer Stadtmauer'. No Mainz tariff is known; only old and just tolls are lawful. The gate and the toll man's seat are a guess (?).
pages.source: Design/content/dossiers/mogontia.md (the research this file is built on; its section 9 has every reference in full)

pages.title: The market inside the gate, Mogontia
pages.hint: A market, not yet seen
pages.brief: A market at Mogontia. A widening of the old street between the wall and the bishop's church: casks on their sides, sacks of Main wheat, stacked pots from downriver, a Frisian with cloaks over his arm.
pages.game: A market at Mogontia. A widening of the old street between the wall and the bishop's church: casks on their sides, sacks of Main wheat, stacked pots from downriver, a Frisian with cloaks over his arm. Roman paving shows through the mud. Hens, a hand-bell, and the new wine sharp in the air after Michaelmas. What is done here: haggle the price, try the goods, weigh the silver, hire carriers and buy stores. Found here: Gundhart.
pages.known: The market's site is unknown: placed by the river gate as a guess.

pages.title: The wine cellars under the wall
pages.hint: A storehouse, not yet seen
pages.brief: A storehouse at Mogontia. Low stone vaults dug into the foot of the wall, older than anyone's grandfather, with casks two deep on oak rails and a boy asleep on the top row.
pages.game: A storehouse at Mogontia. Low stone vaults dug into the foot of the wall, older than anyone's grandfather, with casks two deep on oak rails and a boy asleep on the top row. A tallow lamp, a chalk tally on the door post. Cold, and the smell of a hundred vintages in the stone. What is done here: buy from makers, try the goods, use your store, rent store room and load and unload. Found here: Folcbald.
pages.known: Wine from the country round Mainz. Roman vaults reused as cellars are a guess (?).
pages.source: Design/content/dossiers/mogontia.md (the research this file is built on; its section 9 has every reference in full)

pages.title: The mint by Saint Martin's
pages.hint: A mint, not yet seen
pages.brief: A mint at Mogontia. A stone room with one barred window, a charcoal hearth, an oak block with the lower die set in it and a man holding the upper die while another swings.
pages.game: A mint at Mogontia. A stone room with one barred window, a charcoal hearth, an oak block with the lower die set in it and a man holding the upper die while another swings. A scale hangs from a beam over a cloth. The ring of the hammer comes out into the street a beat late. What is done here: change coin, test the silver and weigh the silver. Found here: Madalger.
pages.known: A penny of Charles's early type (771-794), CARO/LVS, 1.32 g, struck at Mainz: Münzkabinett Berlin, object 18245022. Merovingian moneyers of Mainz: Landesmuseum Mainz, 'Living on the Rhine'. Where the mint stood is a guess.

pages.title: Saint Martin's, the bishop's church
pages.hint: A church, not yet seen
pages.brief: A church at Mogontia. An old stone church among lower roofs, patched with Roman brick, its door open on a dark nave with one lamp at the far end.
pages.game: A church at Mogontia. An old stone church among lower roofs, patched with Roman brick, its door open on a dark nave with one lamp at the far end. Clerks cross the yard with wax tablets. A bell, slow chant at the hours, and beeswax over the smell of the street. What is done here: hear Mass, give alms, make a vow, take sanctuary and fund a work. Found here: Riculf.
pages.known: De.wikipedia 'St. Johannis (Mainz)': the old cathedral; what stood in 793 is unknown, so the look is a guess.
pages.source: Design/content/dossiers/mogontia.md (the research this file is built on; its section 9 has every reference in full)

later.text: De.wikipedia 'St. Johannis (Mainz)': the old cathedral, rebuilt by Hatto about 900.
From about 1000 Willigis's cathedral rises east of it ('Mainzer Dom').

pages.title: The bishop's hall, Mogontia
pages.hint: A hall, not yet seen
pages.brief: A hall at Mogontia. A long timber hall on stone footings beside the church, benches down both walls, a table at the end covered with tablets, tally sticks and one precious ink-horn.
pages.game: A hall at Mogontia. A long timber hall on stone footings beside the church, benches down both walls, a table at the end covered with tablets, tally sticks and one precious ink-horn. Petitioners wait by the door with their caps in their hands. Rush-smoke, wet wool, and a clerk's voice reading a list. What is done here: ask an audience, bring a case, call witnesses, hear the law, give a gift and swear an oath. Found here: Otbert and Brunric.
pages.known: Invented as a building; the archbishop's court and the hostages brought to Mainz at mid-Lent are from the Indiculus obsidum (MGH Capitularia I no. 115) (?).
pages.source: Design/content/dossiers/mogontia.md (the research this file is built on; its section 9 has every reference in full)

later.text: By about 900 the archbishop is lord of the city (regionalgeschichte.net).

pages.title: Saint Alban's on the hill
pages.hint: An abbey, not yet seen
pages.brief: An abbey at Mogontia. South of the wall the road climbs between old graves to a building yard: lime pits, ox-carts of stone, and the walls of a great three-aisled church rising round a small old one.
pages.game: An abbey at Mogontia. South of the wall the road climbs between old graves to a building yard: lime pits, ox-carts of stone, and the walls of a great three-aisled church rising round a small old one. Below, the whole bend of the river and the mouth of the Main. Mason's hammers, then, later, a school reciting. What is done here: hear Mass, have him remembered, bury a man, give alms, read a book, have it copied, fund a work and lodge ashore. Found here: Otbert.
pages.known: Einhard, Translation (tr. Wendell 1926): 'both a church and a very celebrated monastery'.
pages.source: Design/content/dossiers/mogontia.md (the research this file is built on; its section 9 has every reference in full)

later.text: De.wikipedia 'Stift St. Alban vor Mainz': a graveyard since Roman times, Riculf's basilica about 75 m long consecrated 1 December 805, graves of Fastrada (794) and the archbishops.
From 805 it stands whole, fifty paces long.

pages.title: Ratburg's ale-house on the shore
pages.hint: An ale-house, not yet seen
pages.brief: An ale-house at Mogontia. A long low house on a Frisian plot, its door to the river, with a bench outside where haulers sit with their boots off and their feet in a tub.
pages.game: An ale-house at Mogontia. A long low house on a Frisian plot, its door to the river, with a bench outside where haulers sit with their boots off and their feet in a tub. Inside, one hearth, two trestles and a tafl board scratched on a cask head. Ale, onions, wet rope, and three tongues arguing about the price of a tow. What is done here: drink with them, listen for talk, ask the news, throw dice, play tafl, trade riddles, hire a hand and lodge ashore. Found here: Ratburg.
pages.known: Invented; the shore and its people are the Landesmuseum's (From near and far).
pages.source: Design/content/dossiers/mogontia.md (the research this file is built on; its section 9 has every reference in full)

later.text: The house burns with the shore in 886 (Annales Fuldenses).
It stands until about 886.

pages.title: The ferry to Kastel, under the old piers
pages.hint: A ferry, not yet seen
pages.brief: A ferry at Mogontia. A flat ferry barge on a pole at the foot of a lane, and out in the stream twenty-one stone piers in a line to the far bank, each with a bush growing on top and brown water piling against it.
pages.game: A ferry at Mogontia. A flat ferry barge on a pole at the foot of a lane, and out in the stream twenty-one stone piers in a line to the far bank, each with a bush growing on top and brown water piling against it. Beyond, the low walls of the old fort at Kastel. Herons on the piers; the ferryman shouting at a horse. What is done here: cross over, hire a pilot, ask the keeper and listen for talk.
pages.known: De.wikipedia 'Römerbrücke (Mainz)': 21 stone piers, about 600 m; 'Mainz-Kastel'. The ferrymen are named only in modern retellings of the fire.
pages.source: Design/content/dossiers/mogontia.md (the research this file is built on; its section 9 has every reference in full)

later.text: The crossing is by boat: the king's bridge, ten years in the building from about 803, burned in May 813 when it was hardly finished.

pages.title: The king's bridge
pages.hint: A bridge, not yet seen
pages.brief: A bridge at Mogontia.
pages.game: A bridge at Mogontia. New timber going onto the old stone, a little further each year: a roadway of oak beams from the river gate toward Kastel, five hundred paces long when it is done, pale and sharp-edged, with boats passing under between the piers. It smells of fresh-cut oak and tar, and people come out on feast days only to walk on it. What is done here: ask the news and call witnesses.
pages.known: Einhard, Life of Charles 17 and 32 (tr. Turner 1880): five hundred paces, ten years in the building. So the site is a building work until its last spring. Ships passed under it: Notker, Deeds of Charles I.30 (tr. Grant 1905).
pages.source: Design/content/dossiers/mogontia.md (the research this file is built on; its section 9 has every reference in full)

later.text: Einhard, Life of Charles 17 and 32 (tr. Turner 1880): five hundred paces, ten years in the building, burned in three hours in May 813.
In the spring of 813 it is whole, and carts drum across it.
Begun about 803 and finished in 813: de.wikipedia 'Rheinbrücke Karls des Großen' (a reckoning from Einhard's ten years (?)).
It stands until about 813.

pages.title: The potters' row and the pin-makers
pages.hint: A workshop, not yet seen
pages.brief: A workshop at Mogontia. A lane of sheds against the inside of the wall: wheels turning, grey pots drying in rows on planks, a kiln breathing through its roof.
pages.game: A workshop at Mogontia. A lane of sheds against the inside of the wall: wheels turning, grey pots drying in rows on planks, a kiln breathing through its roof. At the end a man casts brooches in a clay mould no bigger than his hand and files them bright. Wood smoke, wet clay, and the click of pots being tried with a knuckle. What is done here: buy from makers, take an order, buy ship's tools and try the goods.
pages.known: Landesmuseum Mainz, 'From near and far': brooches made on the spot, sherds of Badorf and Mayen ware from the shore dig.

later.text: Annales Fuldenses 881 (the potters of Mainz and their pots).

pages.title: The smiths' yard by the south gate
pages.hint: A smithy, not yet seen
pages.brief: A smithy at Mogontia. Three forges under one long roof on the road out to Saint Alban's, horses waiting to be shod, a rack of spurs and bits, and at the back a locked chest the smith does not open for strangers.
pages.game: A smithy at Mogontia. Three forges under one long roof on the road out to Saint Alban's, horses waiting to be shod, a rack of spurs and bits, and at the back a locked chest the smith does not open for strangers. A king's man leans on the gatepost most days and counts who goes in. Hot iron, hoof-parings, hammer and bellows. What is done here: buy ship's tools, take an order and mend the boat.
pages.known: Mounted warriors with fine spurs at Mainz: Landesmuseum Mainz, 'Strategic centre'. The yard is invented; nailed horseshoes are not surely attested before the 9th or 10th century, so horses waiting to be shod in 793 are a guess (?).

pages.hint: A boat yard, not yet seen
pages.brief: A boat yard at Mogontia. Downstream of the jetties the bank is all chips and trestles: a flat barge half planked, a long oak log being hollowed, a raft of Main timber tied to stakes and waiting to be broken up.
pages.game: A boat yard at Mogontia. Downstream of the jetties the bank is all chips and trestles: a flat barge half planked, a long oak log being hollowed, a raft of Main timber tied to stakes and waiting to be broken up. Men caulk with moss and tar. Adzes knock; pitch boils in a pot. What is done here: mend the boat, scrape and tar, order a ship, buy a boat, fit her out and buy ship's tools.
pages.known: The yard itself is a guess.

pages.title: The Drusus stone and the old theatre
pages.hint: A mound, not yet seen
pages.brief: A mound at Mogontia. On the high ground by Saint Alban's road a round stone tower with no door, sixty feet high, older than the wall; below it a great half-bowl of broken seats grown over with elder, and graves dug into its vaults.
pages.game: A mound at Mogontia. On the high ground by Saint Alban's road a round stone tower with no door, sixty feet high, older than the wall; below it a great half-bowl of broken seats grown over with elder, and graves dug into its vaults. Wind in the grass. Boys herd goats where ten thousand once sat. What is done here: have him remembered and ask the news.
pages.known: De.wikipedia 'Drususstein' (a Roman tower-tomb about 20 m high); 'Mogontiacum' (the theatre of about 10,000 seats, graves in its vaults from the 6th century).

pages.title: The spice men by the river gate
pages.hint: A market, not yet seen
pages.brief: A market at Mogontia.
pages.game: A market at Mogontia. Three stalls under one awning, kept by men in long gowns who speak Frankish with a southern lilt and write in letters of their own: small leather bags, a folding scale, a bowl of foreign silver with no king's face on it. Pepper and cloves reach the nose before the eye finds them. What is done here: weigh the silver, test the silver, try the goods and haggle the price. Found here: Liutefred.
pages.known: Jacob 1896: dirhams of Samarkand of 301 and 302 of the Hijra, and pepper, ginger, cloves, spikenard, costus, galangal. Jewish long-distance traders at Mainz from the mid-10th century: de.wikipedia 'Jüdische Gemeinde Mainz'; Landesmuseum Mainz, 'The Jewish community'. The stalls' place is a guess.

pages.title: The port under the wall
pages.hint: A landing, not yet seen
pages.brief: A landing at Namnetis. A strand of timber staging and beached hulls under the long grey river wall, from the Erdre mouth down to Bishop Felix's channel.
pages.game: A landing at Namnetis. A strand of timber staging and beached hulls under the long grey river wall, from the Erdre mouth down to Bishop Felix's channel. In front, flat barges with towing masts and round salt boats from the bay, porters in the mud to their knees; behind, the wall with its round corner tower and one tin roof shining over it. Across the brown water, low islands of willow and sand and the south bank at Reze. A smell of wet salt sacks, river mud and wine lees. What is done here: load and unload, hire carriers, wait for wind, ask the keeper, use your store, rent store room and buy from makers. Found here: Paternus.
pages.known: The city's port and its toll: Chronicon Namnetense c. 14. The Roman port from Richebourg to Port-Maillard and Felix's channel: fr.wikipedia Port de Nantes, Felix de Nantes. The islands: en.wikipedia Nantes. The staging is ours.

pages.title: The toll bench
pages.hint: A toll place, not yet seen
pages.brief: A toll place at Namnetis. A plank bench and a locked chest under a lean-to against the wall, by the gate up from the strand.
pages.game: A toll place at Namnetis. A plank bench and a locked chest under a lean-to against the wall, by the gate up from the strand. A man with a tally stick and a boy with a balance sit facing the boats; carts wait in a line behind, wheels counted as they pass. Everything that comes by ship or any other way stops here first. What is done here: pay the toll, show the charter and weigh the silver. Found here: Nanthard.
pages.known: The toll on all goods coming to the port by ship or any other way, with cart-toll and wheel-toll, gathered by named kinds of men: Chronicon Namnetense c. 14 (857).

later.text: The toll on all goods coming to the port by ship or any other way, with cart-toll and wheel-toll, gathered by named kinds of men: Chronicon Namnetense c. 14 (857), carried back to 793 as the king's and the count's. From about 940 it is split in three: c. 31.

pages.title: The market inside the gate, Namnetis
pages.hint: A market, not yet seen
pages.brief: A market at Namnetis.
pages.game: A market at Namnetis. A wide paved street of the old Roman town, grass between the stones, with trestles down both sides: grey salt in open sacks, casks on their bilges, strings of dried lamprey, baskets of shad on wet leaves, Breton grain, pots. Roofless Roman walls behind serve as pens and stores. Carters shout for room, a clerk's bell rings from the cathedral, and somebody is always frying fish. What is done here: haggle the price, try the goods, buy stores, buy ship's tools and listen for talk. Found here: Maurus.
pages.known: Markets that paid toll: Chronicon Namnetense c. 14. The street and the stalls are ours; the shad and lamprey are the Loire's own fish, not in any text of these years (?).
pages.source: Design/content/dossiers/namnetis.md (the research this file is built on; its tags are written out in each source field)

pages.title: Saints Peter and Paul
pages.hint: A minster, not yet seen
pages.brief: A minster at Namnetis. Bishop Felix's church by the east wall: three naves under a roof of tin, marble columns, walls of small coloured stones, gold crowns hanging over the altars and a great crucifix held from the beam by a silver chain.
pages.game: A minster at Namnetis. Bishop Felix's church by the east wall: three naves under a roof of tin, marble columns, walls of small coloured stones, gold crowns hanging over the altars and a great crucifix held from the beam by a silver chain. On one column sits a red stone from Alexandria that is said to give light at night. Lamp smoke, old incense, the cold of marble; clerks chanting behind a screen. What is done here: hear Mass, give alms, make a vow, take sanctuary, ask the news, read a book and fund a work. Found here: Odilard.
pages.known: Chronicon Namnetense c. 1 (the altars, crowns, crucifix and carbuncle); fr.wikipedia Cathedrale Saint-Pierre-et-Saint-Paul de Nantes (three naves, the tin roof).
pages.source: Design/content/dossiers/namnetis.md (the research this file is built on; its tags are written out in each source field)

later.text: Wrecked 843, rebuilt about 900, burned 919, roofless 937, east end rebuilt 981-988: the eras say which church the player sees.

pages.title: Saint John the Baptist's
pages.hint: A church, not yet seen
pages.brief: A church at Namnetis. A small old church near the cathedral with a basin for baptism sunk in its floor and a porch black with candle smoke.
pages.game: A church at Namnetis. A small old church near the cathedral with a basin for baptism sunk in its floor and a porch black with candle smoke. On most days two clerks and a sweeping woman. On the eve of the saint it cannot be seen for people: pilgrims asleep against the walls, sellers of wax and bread, a vigil that lasts till light. What is done here: hear Mass, make a vow, give alms, listen for talk, lodge ashore and fund a work.
pages.known: The pilgrims' goal on Saint John's day, with a night vigil kept by its clerks: Miracula ecclesiae Namnetensis c. 4; Chronicon Namnetense c. 6 (pilgrims from far cities). It is the church called Saint-Jean-du-Baptistere, built in the 4th or 5th century on the north side of the cathedral and found in the digs of 1910-1913: a baptistery, so the basin follows.

pages.hint: An ale-house, not yet seen
pages.brief: An ale-house at Namnetis. A low room built into the back of the wall beside the gate the carts use, its door open on the street.
pages.game: An ale-house at Namnetis. A low room built into the back of the wall beside the gate the carts use, its door open on the street. Casks on a rack, benches polished by carters, a hearth in the middle with the smoke going out through the thatch, a tally of chalk strokes on a beam. Beyond the back door, a shed stacked with salt sacks. Sour ale, woodsmoke, wet wool, and everybody's business. What is done here: drink with them, listen for talk, throw dice, hire a hand, lodge ashore and trade riddles. Found here: Electa.
pages.known: A gate called Porta Cararia, next to the bishop's postern. The house and its keeper are ours.

later.text: From 836 the keeper of the salt shed behind it holds Aldhelm's riddle of the wine cask.
All the ale-houses of the city paid toll in 857: Chronicon Namnetense c. 14.
A gate called Porta Cararia, next to the bishop's postern, is named about 940: c. 31.

pages.title: The count's house, Namnetis
pages.hint: A hall, not yet seen
pages.brief: A hall at Namnetis. A big Roman house inside the wall, patched with timber, where the count sits when he is in the city: a hall with a painted wall gone pale, spears stacked by the door, hounds, a clerk at a table of wax tablets.
pages.game: A hall at Namnetis. A big Roman house inside the wall, patched with timber, where the count sits when he is in the city: a hall with a painted wall gone pale, spears stacked by the door, hounds, a clerk at a table of wax tablets. Men of the march come and go in riding dress. It is no fortress; the city wall is all the castle there is. What is done here: ask an audience, give a gift, bring a case, swear an oath, call witnesses, hear the law and hold a feast. Found here: Wido.
pages.known: Ours: where the count lived is not known.
pages.source: Design/content/dossiers/namnetis.md (the research this file is built on; its tags are written out in each source field)

later.text: The count as guard of the march: Annales regni Francorum 799.
It stands until about 850.
Ours: where the count lived is not known, and no castle stood before about 900.

later.text: A wall thrown round the cathedral and its houses: first Bishop Fulcher's refuge of about 900, then, on the same line, Alan's great bank of earth with a ditch and a timber tower where he lives.
Chronicon Namnetense c. 26 (Fulcher's walled refuge), c. 28 (it falls, 919), c. 30 (Alan's earthwork and tower, about 940), c. 44.
After 990 a second castle, the Bouffay, stands at the corner by the water, and its men look at this one.

pages.title: The moneyer's house, Namnetis
pages.hint: A mint, not yet seen
pages.brief: A mint at Namnetis. A stone room near the count's house with a barred window: a charcoal hearth, a block with an iron die set in it, a man striking and a man feeding blanks, a third weighing what comes out.
pages.game: A mint at Namnetis. A stone room near the count's house with a barred window: a charcoal hearth, a block with an iron die set in it, a man striking and a man feeding blanks, a third weighing what comes out. The new pennies say NAMNETVM round a cross. Old coin and foreign silver go into the pot at the rate chalked on the door. What is done here: change coin, test the silver and weigh the silver.
pages.known: Pennies of Louis the Pious reading NAMNETVM (1.78 g) and of Charles the Bald reading NAMNETIS CIVITAS (1.62 g): Prou 1896, pp. 92-93. No mint under King Charles the Great.

later.text: No mint under King Charles the Great, so nothing before 814.
It stands until about 877.

pages.hint: An abbey, not yet seen
pages.brief: An abbey at Namnetis. Three leagues below the city, a low green island in the stream with a church, a ring of wooden houses and fish weirs staked out into the current.
pages.game: An abbey at Namnetis. Three leagues below the city, a low green island in the stream with a church, a ring of wooden houses and fish weirs staked out into the current. Monks in the shallows hauling a net, herons, a bell over the water. In the guest house a foreign monk sits among stacked calfskins, writing with his sleeves tied back. It smells of river and smoked fish. What is done here: lodge ashore, hear Mass, give alms, read a book, have it copied, buy from makers and take an order. Found here: Eadhelm.
pages.known: Hermeland's monastery of about 673, three leagues below the city in fish-rich water; fr.wikipedia Hermeland d'Indre. That a monk of Tours lodged there is ours.

later.text: Hermeland's monastery of about 673, three leagues below the city in fish-rich water, burned on 29 June 843 and never rebuilt: Chronicon Namnetense c. 6.
It stands until about 843.

pages.title: Saints Donatian and Rogatian, outside the wall
pages.hint: A graveyard, not yet seen
pages.brief: A graveyard at Namnetis. A basilica among graves on the road east of the city, where the two brothers of Nantes who died for the faith are buried.
pages.game: A graveyard at Namnetis. A basilica among graves on the road east of the city, where the two brothers of Nantes who died for the faith are buried. Stone coffins lie half out of the ground, older ones under them; a chapel of Saint Stephen stands to one side. Nearer the wall is Saint Cyr's little church with its own yard. The city buries its dead here, outside, as the Romans did. Yew, turned earth, a wind off the river. What is done here: bury a man, have him remembered, hear Mass, give alms and make a vow.
pages.known: Fr.wikipedia Basilique Saint-Donatien-et-Saint-Rogatien (four successive churches, Merovingian stone coffins, a pagan cemetery beneath; Saint Stephen's chapel); burial outside the walls at St Donatian's, St Cyr's and St Andrew's: Chronicon Namnetense c. 23; Miracula c. 3.

pages.title: The Reze crossing
pages.hint: A ferry, not yet seen
pages.brief: A ferry at Namnetis. A broad flat boat on a sloping hard at the downstream end of the strand, and the river beyond it split into channels by willow islands.
pages.game: A ferry at Namnetis. A broad flat boat on a sloping hard at the downstream end of the strand, and the river beyond it split into channels by willow islands. The ferryman poles from sandbank to sandbank and rows the deep parts; a cart and two oxen stand aboard looking unhappy. On the far side the old south-bank port, a few roofs among Roman ruin, and the road to the salt country and Herio. What is done here: cross over, hire a pilot, ask the keeper and ask the news. Found here: Paternus.
pages.known: Reze (Ratiatum), the old port on the south bank: fr.wikipedia Reze, Port de Nantes. No bridge is known in 793. The ferry is ours; a Loire ferryman who wants his fare is in Ermentarius.
pages.source: Design/content/dossiers/namnetis.md (the research this file is built on; its tags are written out in each source field)

pages.title: The boat strand on the Erdre
pages.hint: A boat yard, not yet seen
pages.brief: A boat yard at Namnetis. Where the little river comes in under the north-west tower: a muddy bank out of the tide's pull, with a barge on blocks, a boat upside down being tarred, and oak from up the Erdre stacked to season.
pages.game: A boat yard at Namnetis. Where the little river comes in under the north-west tower: a muddy bank out of the tide's pull, with a barge on blocks, a boat upside down being tarred, and oak from up the Erdre stacked to season. Two men with adzes, a boy boiling pitch, shavings everywhere. The wall rises straight behind it. What is done here: mend the boat, scrape and tar, order a ship, buy a boat, fit her out and buy ship's tools.
pages.known: Ours: no shipwright of Nantes is named. The workshops of the city paid toll (Chronicon Namnetense c. 14); the wall ran along the Erdre.

pages.title: The landing under the hill
pages.hint: A landing, not yet seen
pages.brief: A landing at Noviomagus. A shelving bank of grey mud and gravel at the foot of a steep hill, boats drawn up bow first, a few oak posts to tie to.
pages.game: A landing at Noviomagus. A shelving bank of grey mud and gravel at the foot of a steep hill, boats drawn up bow first, a few oak posts to tie to. Behind, a path climbs through alder and bramble to old stone walls on the skyline. The river is wide and brown and loud at the bend; it smells of wet rope, fish scales and wood smoke. What is done here: load and unload, hire carriers, ask the keeper, wait for wind and hire a pilot. Found here: Eilward.
pages.known: The landing at the hill's foot, a harbour since Roman times: de.wikipedia Valkhof. Nothing is recorded of pilots here: the pilot is the ferryman's invented side work (?).
pages.source: Design/content/dossiers/noviomagus.md (the research this file is built on; its tags are given in brackets above)

pages.title: The bank below the wall
pages.hint: A market, not yet seen
pages.brief: A market at Noviomagus. Trestles and upturned baskets on trodden ground between the river and a high wall of grey-brown tuff.
pages.game: A market at Noviomagus. Trestles and upturned baskets on trodden ground between the river and a high wall of grey-brown tuff. Farm wives from the Batua side with cheese and eels, a potter's boy with Rhine pots in straw, sacks of grain under a hide. When the court is in, the crowd is thick and palace servants push to the front; when it is not, six people and a dog. What is done here: haggle the price, try the goods, weigh the silver, buy stores and listen for talk.
pages.known: Invented in detail; merchants, boatmen, craftsmen and farmers in a small settlement on the bank. No market right, fair or toll is recorded: it is a selling place by custom only.
pages.source: Design/content/dossiers/noviomagus.md (the research this file is built on; its tags are given in brackets above)

pages.title: The old wall of tuff
pages.hint: A wall, not yet seen
pages.brief: A wall at Noviomagus. A Roman wall, thick and higher than two men, running along the bank: soft grey stone gone green at the foot, with courses of flat red tile.
pages.game: A wall at Noviomagus. A Roman wall, thick and higher than two men, running along the bank: soft grey stone gone green at the foot, with courses of flat red tile. Lean-to sheds of wattle stand against it. Jackdaws nest in the holes where beams once went. Broken tiles underfoot, some with letters pressed into them. What is done here: rent store room, use your store, throw dice and ask the news.
pages.known: The 4th-century riverside wall of tuff, a stretch of which survives at the Waalkade; the sheds are invented.
pages.source: Design/content/dossiers/noviomagus.md (the research this file is built on; its tags are given in brackets above)

pages.title: The fort gate
pages.hint: A gate, not yet seen
pages.brief: A gate at Noviomagus. At the top of the path an old ditch, half filled, and a gap in a Roman wall closed by a new oak gate.
pages.game: A gate at Noviomagus. At the top of the path an old ditch, half filled, and a gap in a Roman wall closed by a new oak gate. Two spearmen with round shields lean in the shade. Through the gate: scaffolding poles, a heap of cut stone, a white stone capital lying on its side in the straw. Carts wait. A huntsman comes up the hill with a roe deer on a pole. What is done here: give a gift, show the charter, hear the law and ask the news. Found here: Haribrand.
pages.known: The Roman fort with its ditches, inside which the palace stood; three Corinthian capitals of Carrara marble. The gate and its guard are invented.
pages.source: Design/content/dossiers/noviomagus.md (the research this file is built on; its tags are given in brackets above)

later.text: Three Corinthian capitals of Carrara marble, about 775-800.
It stands until about 880.

pages.title: The king's house, Noviomagus
pages.hint: A hall, not yet seen
pages.brief: A hall at Noviomagus. A long stone hall inside the old fort, its roof timbers new, its far end still under scaffolding in the first years.
pages.game: A hall at Noviomagus. A long stone hall inside the old fort, its roof timbers new, its far end still under scaffolding in the first years. Benches along the walls, a raised seat at the east end, hangings where the plaster is unfinished. From the door the whole flat Batua lies open to the north, the river bright across it. It smells of lime, rushes and roast meat on a feast day. What is done here: ask an audience, give a gift, hold a feast, swear an oath, bring a case and call witnesses.
pages.known: The palace of 777, 'a palace of vast size and wonderful work' (Regino 881); the view over the Betuwe. What it looked like is not known: no ground plan survives, and this picture is invention (?).
pages.source: Design/content/dossiers/noviomagus.md (the research this file is built on; its tags are given in brackets above)

pages.game: A workshop at Noviomagus. A small room off the hall with one window to the south. A sloped desk, a bench, horns of ink, a knife, a stack of wax tablets tied with cord, a chest with an iron lock. A young clerk with inky fingers reads a law aloud to himself to find where the scribe before him went wrong. Chalk dust and the smell of sheepskin. What is done here: read a book, have it copied, trade riddles, hear the law and call witnesses. Found here: Engilbald.
pages.known: The room is invented.

later.text: The clerks of the capitularies written here in 806 and 808.
It stands until about 880.

pages.title: The church by the palace
pages.hint: A church, not yet seen
pages.brief: A church at Noviomagus. A plain small hall on the slope below the fort, stone to the height of a man and timber above, with a thatched roof and a wooden cross on the gable.
pages.game: A church at Noviomagus. A plain small hall on the slope below the fort, stone to the height of a man and timber above, with a thatched roof and a wooden cross on the gable. Inside it is dark: one lamp, a stone altar, a painted cloth. Old people of the bank stand at the back. To the west the ground is lumpy with graves nobody tends. What is done here: hear Mass, give alms, make a vow, take sanctuary, bury a man, have him remembered and fund a work. Found here: Liudrad.
pages.known: The parish church by the palace, by tradition Nijmegen's first, of Saint Stephen or Saint Gertrude (the sources disagree), a modest hall of stone or wood; first mentioned in the 15th century and never found (?). The grave fields closed about 700.

pages.hint: A storehouse, not yet seen
pages.brief: A storehouse at Noviomagus. Inside the fort wall, a stone-footed barn and a sunk cellar with a ramp for casks.
pages.game: A storehouse at Noviomagus. Inside the fort wall, a stone-footed barn and a sunk cellar with a ramp for casks. Tally sticks hang in bundles from a beam. A heavy man with keys at his belt counts sacks as they come off a cart, and counts them again. Cool air, the sour smell of wine lees, mice. What is done here: take an order, try the goods, haggle the price, buy from makers and ask the news. Found here: Ratbert.
pages.known: Invented; farms of the later Realm of Nijmegen and the forest toward Xanten fed the court. No steward of Nijmegen is named in the sources.

pages.hint: An ale-house, not yet seen
pages.brief: An ale-house at Noviomagus. A low house of posts and wattle west of the hill, the door facing the river, a bush on a pole above it.
pages.game: An ale-house at Noviomagus. A low house of posts and wattle west of the hill, the door facing the river, a bush on a pole above it. One room, a hearth in the middle with the smoke going out through the thatch, benches, a board scratched for a game. Boatmen with wet leg bindings. A broad woman ladles ale from a tub and listens to everything. What is done here: drink with them, listen for talk, throw dice, play tafl, trade riddles, hire a hand and lodge ashore. Found here: Wendilgard.
pages.known: Invented; the settlement of the 9th and 10th centuries lay west of the hill near the river. The house is kept by her daughters and theirs after her.

pages.hint: A boat yard, not yet seen

pages.game: A boat yard at Noviomagus. Downstream of the landing, a flat-bottomed barge half built on blocks, its oak bottom planks wider than a man's chest. Two men with adzes, a boy boiling moss and tar in an iron pot. Split logs stacked to season, a log boat hauled out with a cracked side. Chips everywhere, and the sweet sharp smell of cut oak. What is done here: mend the boat, scrape and tar, buy a boat, order a ship, fit her out and buy ship's tools.
pages.known: Invented; river craft of the Rhine branches; the capitulary of 808 has a heading on the ships ordered built.

pages.title: The Batua crossing
pages.hint: A ferry, not yet seen
pages.brief: A ferry at Noviomagus. A broad punt on a pole, grounded where a cart track comes down to the water.
pages.game: A ferry at Noviomagus. A broad punt on a pole, grounded where a cart track comes down to the water. Across the brown river the far bank is a low green line of willow and reed, with cattle on it and nothing higher than a hayrick as far as the eye goes. A net dries on stakes. The ferryman sits mending it and watches the current, not you. What is done here: cross over, ask the news, buy from makers and wait for wind. Found here: Eilward.
pages.known: Invented; the Waal 'washes the south side of the island of the Batavians' (Einhard 17, Turner 1880); fishermen in the settlement.

pages.game: A wall at Noviomagus. A bank of fresh earth and a fence of sharpened timber round the whole hilltop, the palace roofs behind it. Long ships drawn up under the hill where the landing was, shields along their sides. Snow on the ground, smoke from many fires, and across the frozen fields the tents of a king's army that cannot get in. What is done here: ask the news, haggle the price, give a gift and call witnesses. Found here: Eberhard.
pages.known: 'A very strong rampart and walls' round Nijmegen; Regino 881. No leader of these Northmen is named.

later.text: 'A very strong rampart and walls' round Nijmegen, the hard winter and the failed siege: Annales Fuldenses 880.

pages.game: A hall at Noviomagus. The old fort walls, and inside them a hall with new roofs on fire-blackened stone. In the Saxon kings' time it is whole again and hung with cloth. What is done here: ask an audience, give a gift, hold a feast, swear an oath, bring a case, call witnesses, hear the law and hear Mass.
pages.known: How and when it was rebuilt is not recorded (?). The chapel's dedication to Saint Nicholas is first written in 1470.

later.text: Burned 881, in use again by 898, courts of the Ottonian and Salian kings, the chapel about 1030-1040, burned 1047.
From about 1030 an eight-sided chapel of grey tuff stands in the yard, with red Roman tiles in its walls.
After 1047 the hall is a scorched shell once more and only the chapel has a roof.

pages.title: The strand under the farm
pages.hint: A beach, not yet seen
pages.brief: A beach at Ögvaldsnes. A grey shingle beach in a narrow sound, ships drawn up bow first with their striped ship-tents pitched ashore beside them.
pages.game: A beach at Ögvaldsnes. A grey shingle beach in a narrow sound, ships drawn up bow first with their striped ship-tents pitched ashore beside them. Behind, a turf slope climbs to the long roof of the hall and a tall leaning stone; across the water the mainland is a low dark line. Oystercatchers, the knock of a mallet, peat smoke, tar and wet kelp. In the morning an old man walks down the path to ask who commands. What is done here: load and unload, scrape and tar, wait for wind, ask the keeper, hire a pilot, hire a hand and buy stores. Found here: Ofeig.
pages.known: Heimskringla, Saint Olaf's saga 123: ships lie below the farm, crews under ship-tents, the lord's man comes down in the morning. No jetty is known before the 1100s.
pages.source: Design/content/dossiers/ogvaldsnes.md (6 Oct 2026): everything marked (?) or late there is marked (?) or (saga) here.

later.text: Heimskringla, Saint Olaf's saga 123 (saga, of 1022): ships lie below the farm, crews under ship-tents, the lord's man comes down in the morning.

pages.title: The hall on the ness
pages.hint: A hall, not yet seen
pages.brief: A hall at Ögvaldsnes. One long room under a turf roof, a fire down the middle and smoke hanging in the rafters.
pages.game: A hall at Ögvaldsnes. One long room under a turf roof, a fire down the middle and smoke hanging in the rafters. Benches run along both walls with the high seat in the middle of the north side; shields and a striped sail hang behind it. Women with keys at their belts carry ale; thralls who speak the islands' tongue keep the fire. It smells of smoke, wet wool, dogs and boiled meat, and somebody is always halfway through a story. What is done here: ask an audience, give a gift, hold a feast, swear an oath, ask the news, listen for talk, pay the singer and trade riddles, and more. Found here: Thorleif, Gunnhild and Hallgrim.
pages.known: The high seat and ante-room are Saint Olaf's saga 124. Gaming pieces of amber and glass lay in the mound of 779.

pages.title: The lord's store
pages.hint: A storehouse, not yet seen
pages.brief: A storehouse at Ögvaldsnes. A squat log house on stone footings beside the hall, its door bound with iron and a woman's key in the lock.
pages.game: A storehouse at Ögvaldsnes. A squat log house on stone footings beside the hall, its door bound with iron and a woman's key in the lock. Inside, in the half dark: soapstone pots nested in hay, bundles of grey whetstones, bar iron, sacks of down, corn bins, and on one shelf the odd things from over the sea. A folding scale hangs by the door. This is as near to a market as the place has: you deal with whoever holds the key. What is done here: haggle the price, weigh the silver, test the silver, try the goods, give a gift and use your store. Found here: Gunnhild.
pages.known: No market is recorded here: goods changed hands with the lord or his bailiff. The goods are the region's, not proven for this farm.
pages.source: Design/content/dossiers/ogvaldsnes.md (6 Oct 2026): everything marked (?) or late there is marked (?) or (saga) here.

later.text: 'Great corn stacks' at the farm in 1022 (Saint Olaf's saga 123, saga).

pages.title: The workshop ground
pages.hint: A workshop, not yet seen
pages.brief: A workshop at Ögvaldsnes. A trampled yard south of the hall, black with charcoal.
pages.game: A workshop at Ögvaldsnes. A trampled yard south of the hall, black with charcoal. A smith works under an open lean-to with a boy at the bellows; beyond him grain dries on a clay floor over a slow fire, and at the shore a thrall feeds driftwood under a pan of sea water crusted white. Hammer on iron, the hiss of the quench, the bitter smell of burnt seaweed and hot salt. What is done here: buy ship's tools, take an order, fit her out, buy from makers and fund a work.

later.text: The workshop area: forging, handicraft, grain drying and salt making, in use about 200 to 1000 (Nordvegen History Centre, research page).
It stands until about 1000.

pages.title: The boat shore, Ögvaldsnes
pages.hint: A boat yard, not yet seen
pages.brief: A boat yard at Ögvaldsnes. North of the strand a long low boat-house of turf and stone opens straight on the water, a hull on rollers inside it and another half built beside it under the sky.
pages.game: A boat yard at Ögvaldsnes. North of the strand a long low boat-house of turf and stone opens straight on the water, a hull on rollers inside it and another half built beside it under the sky. Split oak planks lie stacked with sticks between them; a trough steams. A lean man sights along a strake and says nothing. Wood shavings, tar pots, wool yarn for caulking, and the sound of an adze that never hurries. What is done here: mend the boat, scrape and tar, order a ship, buy a boat, fit her out and fund a work. Found here: Odd.
pages.known: The ships in the mounds: an oak ship of about 27 m (779) and a boat of about 15 m built about 780. Shipwrights are inferred from them.
pages.source: Design/content/dossiers/ogvaldsnes.md (6 Oct 2026): everything marked (?) or late there is marked (?) or (saga) here.

pages.title: The Great Mound
pages.hint: A mound, not yet seen
pages.brief: A mound at Ögvaldsnes. A round green hill made by hands, fifty paces across and three men high, on the ridge north of the farm with the whole sound below it.
pages.game: A mound at Ögvaldsnes. A round green hill made by hands, fifty paces across and three men high, on the ridge north of the farm with the whole sound below it. Sheep graze its sides. From the top you see every sail between the two ends of the strait. The wind never drops here, and men lower their voices without being asked. What is done here: have him remembered, make an offering, cast the lots and make a vow.
pages.known: Storhaug at Gunnarshaug: 40-50 m across, 5-6 m high, the ship burial of summer 779 (Nordvegen History Centre). The man in it is named in no text; do not call him a king by name.
pages.source: Design/content/dossiers/ogvaldsnes.md (6 Oct 2026): everything marked (?) or late there is marked (?) or (saga) here.

pages.hint: A mound, not yet seen

pages.game: A mound at Ögvaldsnes. A second mound a little north of the first, lower and steeper, its turf still showing the cut lines of the sods in its first years. A boat lies under it with her stem to the south. For some summers a pole with a strip of red cloth stands on the top; later only the grass, and the name. What is done here: have him remembered, make an offering, call witnesses and fund a work.
pages.known: Gronhaug at Bo: about 30 m across and 4 m high, a boat of about 15 m, a man's burial of 790-795 by tree rings.

pages.title: The stone and the two mounds
pages.hint: A shrine, not yet seen
pages.brief: A shrine at Ögvaldsnes. Beside the hall a grey stone taller than four men leans a little, like a mast in a swell.
pages.game: A shrine at Ögvaldsnes. Beside the hall a grey stone taller than four men leans a little, like a mast in a swell. Either side of it stand two more mounds, a great one and a lesser that the farm people call the cow mound. At the feasts the stone's foot is dark and wet and the ground is trodden. Children are told not to climb; they climb. What is done here: make an offering, swear an oath, make a vow, cast the lots, hold a feast and hear the law. Found here: Alof.
pages.known: The standing stone, 7.2 m: older than the church, its age not found (?). Flaghaug, 43 m across, and Kjellerhaug or Kuhaugen, 'the cow mound'. The stone's Mary name is Christian and later: nobody uses it here. King Ogvald and his cow: Olaf Trygvason's saga 71 (saga). Offerings at the stone are the game's.
pages.source: Design/content/dossiers/ogvaldsnes.md (6 Oct 2026): everything marked (?) or late there is marked (?) or (saga) here.

pages.title: The heath of the old mounds
pages.hint: A field, not yet seen
pages.brief: A field at Ögvaldsnes. Above the farm the land rises to bare heather and bog cotton, and along the skyline stands a row of low mounds older than anyone's reckoning.
pages.game: A field at Ögvaldsnes. Above the farm the land rises to bare heather and bog cotton, and along the skyline stands a row of low mounds older than anyone's reckoning. Swine root between them, watched by boys with sticks. The open sea is grey to the west, the sound bright to the east. Wind, curlews, the grunt of pigs; in the king's years a stack of dry wood stands ready on the highest point. What is done here: ask the news, have him remembered, buy from makers and fund a work. Found here: Cuthred.
pages.known: Rehaugane, the row of Bronze Age mounds on the heights.
pages.source: Design/content/dossiers/ogvaldsnes.md (6 Oct 2026): everything marked (?) or late there is marked (?) or (saga) here.

later.text: The battle of 953 among them, Blodeheia: Hakon the Good's saga 20 (saga).

pages.title: The skerries in the sound
pages.hint: A fishery, not yet seen
pages.brief: A fishery at Ögvaldsnes. Low black rocks off the ness, wet to their tops at flood tide, white with birds.
pages.game: A fishery at Ögvaldsnes. Low black rocks off the ness, wet to their tops at flood tide, white with birds. A man in a skin boat works along them with a net on a pole and a basket for eggs; seals watch him from the far side. Past them the channel narrows until two ships cannot pass without the crews seeing each other's faces. What is done here: buy from makers, hire a pilot, cast the lots and wait for wind.
pages.known: The narrow passage along Avaldsnes. Skrattasker, the skerry 'under water in flood tide': Olaf Trygvason's saga 70 (saga); which rock it is, is local tradition (?).
pages.source: Design/content/dossiers/ogvaldsnes.md (6 Oct 2026): everything marked (?) or late there is marked (?) or (saga) here.

pages.title: The king's church
pages.hint: A church, not yet seen
pages.brief: A church at Ögvaldsnes. A small church of upright timbers and a shingle roof, close by the hall with a trodden path between the two doors.
pages.game: A church at Ögvaldsnes. A small church of upright timbers and a shingle roof, close by the hall with a trodden path between the two doors. The great stone leans toward its wall as if listening. Inside, one window, an altar with a cloth, a priest whose Norse has an English turn. Wax, damp wood, and on feast days more men outside than in. What is done here: hear Mass, give alms, make a vow, take sanctuary, bury a man, ask the news and fund a work.
pages.known: A wooden church is credited to Olaf Tryggvason without proof; no trace has been reported (?). English priests: Hakon's and the Olafs' bishops came from England.
pages.source: Design/content/dossiers/ogvaldsnes.md (6 Oct 2026): everything marked (?) or late there is marked (?) or (saga) here.

later.text: The year 998 is the game's, from his Easter here.
A church stands by the hall with a path to it at Easter 1023 (Saint Olaf's saga 127, saga).

pages.title: The strand under the island wall
pages.hint: A landing, not yet seen
pages.brief: A landing at Parisius. A strip of grey mud and river gravel between the water and an old stone wall twice a man's height, boats drawn up bow first and wine casks rolled on planks.
pages.game: A landing at Parisius. A strip of grey mud and river gravel between the water and an old stone wall twice a man's height, boats drawn up bow first and wine casks rolled on planks. Behind the wall, tiled roofs and the long ridge of the great church at the island's east end. The river is wide, slow and green-brown; it smells of wet oak, lees and cook-fires, and the carters shout in Romance. What is done here: load and unload, hire carriers, ask the keeper, wait for wind, hire a pilot, mend the boat and buy a boat.
pages.known: The 4th-century wall set 15 to 30 m back from the water, so that boats can land under it at low water. Where boats really lay is not recorded: the charter of 753 says only 'ports' (Tardif no. 55).
pages.source: Design/content/dossiers/parisius.md (the research this file rests on; its section 8 lists what is not known and must not be claimed)

pages.title: The Great Bridge
pages.hint: A bridge, not yet seen
pages.brief: A bridge at Parisius. A long timber bridge on piles from the island to the right bank, loud with carts and pack beasts, the water sliding dark between the posts.
pages.game: A bridge at Parisius. A long timber bridge on piles from the island to the right bank, loud with carts and pack beasts, the water sliding dark between the posts. On the far side a round church inside a ditch and a road going north to the saint. What is done here: cross over, pay the toll, show the charter and listen for talk.
pages.known: Two timber bridges, north and south; Charles the Bald's new Great Bridge and its stone tower. Saint-Germain-le-Rond, round and ringed by a ditch. The wheel, bridge and gate tolls are the abbey's during the fair (Tardif no. 77).
pages.source: Design/content/dossiers/parisius.md (the research this file rests on; its section 8 lists what is not known and must not be claimed)

later.text: From the 870s the bridge is the king's new one, low enough to stop a ship, with a stone tower at its bank end that is still unfinished when the great fleet comes.
No towers before the 870s.
Charles the Bald's new Great Bridge and its stone tower, unfinished in November 885.

pages.title: The market between the palace and the church
pages.hint: A market, not yet seen
pages.brief: A market at Parisius. A trodden open place in the middle of the island: trestles of leeks, cheeses, salt fish and bread, wine sold by the jug from a cask on a cart, a woman with baskets of blue dye balls.
pages.game: A market at Parisius. A trodden open place in the middle of the island: trestles of leeks, cheeses, salt fish and bread, wine sold by the jug from a cask on a cart, a woman with baskets of blue dye balls. At the west end the grey mass of the count's house, at the east the church roofs. Pigs, bells, and a crier giving the count's orders in two tongues. What is done here: haggle the price, try the goods, weigh the silver, buy stores, listen for talk and hire a hand.
pages.known: Palace at the west end, the bishop's churches at the east, a market between.
