later.text: Fourteen in 826, a woman of twenty-four in the year of the fire and old after it: dark hair cut to the neck, a burn scar on the left forearm, her grandmother's sticks at her belt, some of them charred at one end.

The burning from Annales Fuldenses 836 (no leader named, and what burned is not known: that the church burned is tradition and our choice); Dorestad plundered 834-836 (Annales Bertiniani); Walcheren given to Harald in 841 (Annales Bertiniani).

pages.title: Hartbert
pages.hint: A shipwright, not yet met
pages.brief: Hartbert, the shipwright at Andoverpis. A carpenter who builds boats when there is oak and houses when there is not, and set the post rows under the bank.
pages.game: Hartbert is the shipwright at Andoverpis, a Frank and a Christian. Found at: the south inlet and the bank and the log paths. A carpenter who builds boats when there is oak and houses when there is not, and set the post rows under the bank.
pages.known: Not in the record: the game's own person, set in a real place. The Roman coin of Constans found in the rampart (Bellens); Meuse ware outweighing Rhenish in the 10th century (Bellens). That householders owed a stretch of the bank is ours (?).
pages.source: T. Bellens, Het DNA van stadswording. De vroeg-stedelijke nederzetting van Antwerpen, late 9de-11de eeuw (2021), chapters 2.2-2.8: https://oar.onroerenderfgoed.be/publicaties/SYNT/5/SYNT005-001.pdf

later.text: Flanders builds forts in the 880s.
Broad in the shoulder, thirty in 898, sandy beard, a leather apron over a short tunic, an adze through his belt and a knotted measuring cord round his neck.
The palisade and bank of about 900, 13.5 m wide, and the long narrow plots from Bellens 2021.
Rollo at Rouen from 911.

pages.title: Gothelo
pages.hint: A count, not yet met
pages.brief: Gothelo, the count at Andoverpis. The margrave: a lord of the eastern kingdom set on a river bank to watch Flanders, and later duke of all Lotharingia.
pages.game: Gothelo is the count at Andoverpis, a Frank and a Christian. Found at: the margrave's hall. The margrave: a lord of the eastern kingdom set on a river bank to watch Flanders, and later duke of all Lotharingia. To look at: seldom without a hound at his knee.
pages.known: A real person. The charter of 1008, 'the county of Count Gozilo, which is called Antwerf' (Mertens and Torfs I, 1845). No visit of his to the place is recorded: that a merchant finds him in his hall here is ours (?). The words are ours.
pages.source: T. Bellens, Het DNA van stadswording. De vroeg-stedelijke nederzetting van Antwerpen, late 9de-11de eeuw (2021), chapters 2.2-2.8: https://oar.onroerenderfgoed.be/publicaties/SYNT/5/SYNT005-001.pdf

later.text: Gothelo I, about 967 to 19 April 1044, margrave of Antwerp from 1005 or 1008, duke of Lower Lotharingia from 1023 and of Upper from 1033.
A heavy man in his forties in 1008, grey later, a long dark-blue cloak with a gold pin, a sword with a silver-wound hilt, riding boots.
Oak piles of 1007-1015 and Tournai stone (Bellens 2021).
Died in 1044.

pages.title: Gerburg
pages.hint: An alewife, not yet met
pages.brief: Gerburg, the alewife at Andoverpis. Keeps the old ale-house, which now stands outside the wall, and the oldest tally sticks on the river, some of them charred.
pages.game: Gerburg is the alewife at Andoverpis, a Frank and a Christian. Found at: the house on posts. Keeps the old ale-house, which now stands outside the wall, and the oldest tally sticks on the river, some of them charred.

later.text: Sea fishing after 1000 (Bellens).
A spare woman, twenty-two in 1022 and white-haired by the siege, a blue wool gown with a woven band, a ring of keys and a bundle of very old sticks in a leather case at her belt.
Cnut's peace 1016-1035.
The siege of 1055 and the burning of the houses round the castle (Mertens and Torfs I, p. 135, after Sigebert).

pages.title: Cuthgar
pages.hint: A king's man, not yet met
pages.brief: Cuthgar, the king's man at Bebbanburg. The thegn who keeps the gate: exact, hard on his men and harder on himself; he had the watch on the eighth of June and saw the sails.
pages.game: Cuthgar is the king's man at Bebbanburg, one of the English and a Christian. Found at: the cleft gate. The thegn who keeps the gate: exact, hard on his men and harder on himself; he had the watch on the eighth of June and saw the sails. To look at: thirty-five, lean, fair hair tied back, a clipped beard, a grey cloak with a bronze ring pin; a spear always in his hand and a shield with a mended board slung behind him.
pages.known: Not in the record: the game's own person, set in a real place. The watch, the forty men and the lack of boats are the game's; only the line of sight to Lindisfarne is real. The riddle paraphrases Exeter riddle 5; the saying turns Durham Proverbs, 'Earh maeg thaet an thaet he him ondraede' (own rendering).

pages.title: Eanwine
pages.hint: A steward, not yet met
pages.brief: Eanwine, the steward at Bebbanburg. Keeper of the household's stores for three kings running: careful, unhurried, loyal to the larder before any lord.
pages.game: Eanwine is the steward at Bebbanburg, one of the English and a Christian. Found at: the steward's board. Keeper of the household's stores for three kings running: careful, unhurried, loyal to the larder before any lord. To look at: nearing fifty, stout, bald on top with a grey fringe, a good brown tunic gone shiny at the belly, a bundle of tally sticks on a thong and keys at his belt.
pages.known: Not in the record: the game's own person, set in a real place. A king's household lived on food-rents (feorm). No steward, market or merchant is recorded at Bamburgh. The first styca of good silver 'c. 790 onwards': Bamburgh Research Project, History of the Northumbrian styca. The saying is Durham Proverbs, 'Gethyld byth middes eades' (own rendering), with his own tail.

pages.title: Wilgar
pages.hint: A priest, not yet met
pages.brief: Wilgar, the priest at Bebbanburg. Mass-priest of Saint Peter's and keeper of the hand; schooled at Lindisfarne, gentle, stubborn about the shrine's rights.
pages.game: Wilgar is the priest at Bebbanburg, one of the English and a Christian. Found at: Saint Peter's and the hand. Mass-priest of Saint Peter's and keeper of the hand; schooled at Lindisfarne, gentle, stubborn about the shrine's rights. To look at: past fifty, thin, tonsured, a darned wool habit and a stole kept very clean; ink on one thumb and the shrine's small key on a cord round his neck.
pages.known: Not in the record: the game's own person, set in a real place. The priests of the hilltop church are shown by Symeon's annal of 774. The dish and the blessing: Bede III.6 (paraphrased). The saying is Durham Proverbs, 'Ne deah eall soth asaed ne eall sar aetwiten' (own rendering).
pages.source: Design/content/dossiers/bebbanburg.md (the research this file is built on, with its own source list)

pages.title: Garmund
pages.hint: A smith, not yet met
pages.brief: Garmund, the smith at Bebbanburg. The king's sword-smith: welds blades of twisted rods as his father did, slow, proud, deaf in one ear from the anvil.
pages.game: Garmund is the smith at Bebbanburg, one of the English and a Christian. Found at: the smiths' ward. The king's sword-smith: welds blades of twisted rods as his father did, slow, proud, deaf in one ear from the anvil. To look at: forty-three, short and very broad, forearms scarred with sparks, hair singed off at the front, a leather apron to the shins and tongs hooked in his belt.
pages.known: Not in the record: the game's own person, set in a real place. The riddle paraphrases Exeter riddle 20; the proverb of the sooty bag is Durham Proverbs, 'Oft on sotigum bylige searowa licgath' (own rendering); his own saying is invented in the period's manner.

pages.title: Bacga
pages.hint: A pilot, not yet met
pages.brief: Bacga, the pilot at Bebbanburg. Fisherman of the inlet and the only man who will take a strange boat through the Farnes in fog; cheerful, superstitious, a great liar about the size of seals.
pages.game: Bacga is the pilot at Bebbanburg, one of the English and a Christian. Found at: the inlet under the rock. Fisherman of the inlet and the only man who will take a strange boat through the Farnes in fog; cheerful, superstitious, a great liar about the size of seals. To look at: thirty-three, wiry, wind-red face, a sealskin cap and jerkin, bare feet with toes spread like a duck's; a gutting knife on a cord and fish scales in his beard.
pages.known: Not in the record: the game's own person, set in a real place. The Megstone is a modern name for an outlying rock (?). The saying is Maxims I, 'Werig sceal se with winde roweth' (own rendering) (?).
pages.source: Design/content/dossiers/bebbanburg.md (the research this file is built on, with its own source list)

pages.title: Muirenn
pages.hint: A widow, not yet met
pages.brief: Muirenn, the widow at Bebbanburg. Born in the western isles, brought here as a king's man's wife forty years ago; brews the vill's ale, lays out the dead and tends the grave field in the sand.
pages.game: Muirenn is the widow at Bebbanburg, a Gael and a Christian. Found at: the vill below the rock. Born in the western isles, brought here as a king's man's wife forty years ago; brews the vill's ale, lays out the dead and tends the grave field in the sand. To look at: nearly sixty, small and straight, white hair under a linen kerchief, a checked shawl pinned with an old ring-brooch from the west; hands stained brown with malt.
pages.known: Not in the record: the game's own person, set in a real place. The Bowl Hole dead came from western Scotland, Ireland, Scandinavia and the Mediterranean, tall, robust, with terrible teeth: Bamburgh Research Project, Bowl Hole. Farthings did not exist: she means a quarter of a cut penny's worth (?). The saying is Durham Proverbs, 'Aet thearfe mann sceal freonda cunnian' (own rendering), with her own tail.

pages.title: Waltheof
pages.hint: A count, not yet met
pages.brief: Waltheof, a count at Bebbanburg. Ealdorman of the old house, lord of everything between Tees and Tweed; outlived his strength and the sack of his own rock.
pages.game: Waltheof is a count at Bebbanburg, one of the English and a Christian. Found at: the hall on the rock. Ealdorman of the old house, lord of everything between Tees and Tweed; outlived his strength and the sack of his own rock. To look at: very old, big-framed and wasted, white beard to the chest, a fur-lined cloak in all weathers, a gold arm-ring grown loose; sits in the carved stone seat with a stick across his knees.
pages.known: A real person. 'Much spoil was there taken': Anglo-Saxon Chronicle 993; the comet is our colour (?). The saying is Durham Proverbs, 'Man deth swa he byth thonne he mot swa he wile' (own rendering).
pages.source: Design/content/dossiers/bebbanburg.md (the research this file is built on, with its own source list)

later.text: His birth, death and the years 975 to 1006 are our frame (?).

pages.title: Uhtred
pages.hint: A count, not yet met
pages.brief: Uhtred, a count at Bebbanburg. Waltheof's son: quick, open-handed, hard; breaks the Scots at Durham and is made earl of all Northumbria; marries three times, each time upward.
pages.game: Uhtred is a count at Bebbanburg, one of the English and a Christian. Found at: the hall on the rock. Waltheof's son: quick, open-handed, hard; breaks the Scots at Durham and is made earl of all Northumbria; marries three times, each time upward. To look at: in his thirties, tall, red-brown hair and moustache, a blue cloak with a gold brooch, rings on both arms; a hawk on his fist or a horn in it, never still.
pages.known: A real person. The man-prices: Northleoda laga. Nothing here is taken from any modern novel. The saying is Durham Proverbs, 'Freond deah feor ge neah: byth near nyttra' (own rendering).
pages.source: Design/content/dossiers/bebbanburg.md (the research this file is built on, with its own source list)

later.text: Active from about 995, when he helped clear the ground at Durham (?).
Died in 1016.

pages.title: Eanmund
pages.hint: A reeve, not yet met
pages.brief: Eanmund, the reeve at Bebbanburg. Reeve of the rock for whichever king the Danes allow beyond the Tyne: heavy, careful, a keeper of keys who has outlasted three lords by never choosing one aloud.

Reeve of the rock for whichever king the Danes allow beyond the Tyne: heavy, careful, a keeper of keys who has outlasted three lords by never choosing one aloud. To look at: past forty, heavy, grey in a brown beard, a brown cloak with a plain bronze pin, a great ring of keys, a tally stick worn smooth.
pages.known: Not in the record: the game's own person, set in a real place. Name: Ean- + -mund.

later.text: After 21 March 867 one Ecgberht reigned under the Danes over the Northumbrians beyond the Tyne; Halfdan wintered on the Tyne in 875 (Symeon of Durham, Historia regum 867, 875).

pages.title: Wulfmaer
pages.hint: A reeve, not yet met
pages.brief: Wulfmaer, the reeve at Bebbanburg. Reeve of the rock for earls who never come: a practical sheep-master with an English name and a Danish lord, who collects the rent and keeps the wall mended out of habit.
pages.game: Wulfmaer is the reeve at Bebbanburg, one of the English and a Christian. Found at: the steward's board. Reeve of the rock for earls who never come: a practical sheep-master with an English name and a Danish lord, who collects the rent and keeps the wall mended out of habit. To look at: fifty, weathered, a clipped grey beard, a sheepskin jerkin over a russet tunic, a horn at his belt and a shepherd's crook that he uses as a staff of office.
pages.known: Not in the record: the game's own person, set in a real place. Name: Wulf- + -maer.

later.text: Siward held all Northumbria after 1041; Malcolm of the Scots ravaged the earldom and broke Cuthbert's peace in 1061; in 1065 Morcar gave the land beyond the Tyne to Oswulf of the old house (Symeon of Durham, Historia regum and the tract on the earls).

pages.title: Holmfast
pages.hint: A merchant, not yet met
pages.brief: Holmfast, the merchant at Birka. Counts everything twice and weighs it a third time: furs east to west, silver west to east, and no word wasted on either.
pages.game: Holmfast is the merchant at Birka, one of the Svear and one who keeps the old gods. Found at: the lanes of the Black Earth and the strangers' booths. Counts everything twice and weighs it a third time: furs east to west, silver west to east, and no word wasted on either. To look at: about thirty-five in 793, spare, pale-eyed, a trimmed beard, a fur-trimmed cap and a belted coat of eastern cut, folding scales in a round bronze case and a bag of lead weights at his belt.
pages.known: Not in the record: the game's own person, set in a real place. Men of Birka had been to Dorstadt (Rimbert 27); scales and weights lie in Birka's graves; partners in one ship were félagar (Magnus 1999). His son keeps the booth after him: the role forge makes the heir. Name: Holm- + -fast, both common on the rune stones of Uppland.
pages.source: Design/content/dossiers/birka.md (6 Oct 2026): the research this file is built on; its section 8 lists what must not be claimed.

pages.title: Grimulf
pages.hint: A skald, not yet met
pages.brief: Grimulf, the skald at Birka. A hall poet grown too hoarse for halls, who sells riddles and verses for weighed silver in the brewing-woman's house and remembers every face that ever paid him.
pages.game: Grimulf is the skald at Birka, one of the Svear and one who keeps the old gods. Found at: the brewing-woman's house. A hall poet grown too hoarse for halls, who sells riddles and verses for weighed silver in the brewing-woman's house and remembers every face that ever paid him. To look at: past sixty, tall and stooped, a long grey moustache and a shaved chin, an old blue cloak pinned with a ring of iron, a bundle of rune-cut sticks tied with bast under his arm.
pages.known: Not in the record: the game's own person, set in a real place. The riddles are Gestumblindi's, from the saga of King Heidrek (Vigfusson and Powell 1883). Name: Grim- + -ulf.
pages.source: Design/content/dossiers/birka.md (6 Oct 2026): the research this file is built on; its section 8 lists what must not be claimed.

later.text: After 828 the role forge makes another skald.

pages.title: Ragnvi
pages.hint: A craftsman, not yet met
pages.brief: Ragnvi, the craftsman at Birka. A bead-maker with her own scale and her own silver, who can tell where a glass rod was drawn by the colour it turns in the fire.
pages.game: Ragnvi is the craftsman at Birka, one of the Svear and one who keeps the old gods. Found at: the casters' and comb-makers' sheds. A bead-maker with her own scale and her own silver, who can tell where a glass rod was drawn by the colour it turns in the fire. To look at: about thirty in 793, small, strong forearms scarred with old burns, hair tied in a cloth, a strap dress on two plain oval brooches with a string of her own beads between them, a little folding balance on a cord.
pages.known: Not in the record: the game's own person, set in a real place. Bead-makers, glass rods, Ribe's 'wasp beads' in the oldest layers, women who owned weights and silver. Name: Ragn- + -vi.

pages.title: Fastlög
pages.hint: A weaver, not yet met
pages.brief: Fastlög, the weaver at Birka. Weaves patterned ribbon on a slotted antler comb for the edges of rich men's coats, and takes in a stranger's mending with the same care.
pages.game: Fastlög is the weaver at Birka, one of the Svear and one who keeps the old gods. Found at: the lanes of the Black Earth. Weaves patterned ribbon on a slotted antler comb for the edges of rich men's coats, and takes in a stranger's mending with the same care. To look at: in her late twenties in 793, broad and calm, fair hair knotted under a linen cloth, a blue strap dress with bronze oval brooches, a needle case and shears hanging from one of them, a narrow band of half-woven ribbon tied to her belt.
pages.known: Not in the record: the game's own person, set in a real place. Weavers and seamstresses (needle cases in the graves), bands woven for coats of eastern cut. Her daughters keep the loom after her. Name: Fast- + -lög.

pages.title: Herigar
pages.hint: A harbour master, not yet met
pages.brief: Herigar, the harbour master at Birka. The keeper of the town and a counsellor of the king: baptised, with a church on his own land, blunt as a judge, and not to be shouted down at the thing.
pages.game: Herigar is the harbour master at Birka, one of the Svear and a Christian. Found at: the stone-footed jetties and the long house on the terrace. The keeper of the town and a counsellor of the king: baptised, with a church on his own land, blunt as a judge, and not to be shouted down at the thing. To look at: lame in one leg for a time, and then not.
pages.known: A real person. Rimbert, Vita Anskarii 11, 19 (tr. Robinson 1921): 'the prefect of this town named Herigar, who was a counsellor of the king'; the wager in the rain, the lame leg, the ransom. His birth year is the game's guess (?). The ties to people of other ports are invented.
pages.source: Design/content/dossiers/birka.md (6 Oct 2026): the research this file is built on; its section 8 lists what must not be claimed.

later.text: About fifty in the 840s, heavy, a grey beard, a fur-trimmed cloak with a ring pin, a small silver cross worn openly, a staff of office and storehouse keys.
Died in 851.
He died about 851.

pages.title: Frideburg
pages.hint: A widow, not yet met
pages.brief: Frideburg, the widow at Birka. Rich, old and unbending: with no priest left in the town she keeps bought wine by her for three years, to be dropped in her mouth at the last.
pages.game: Frideburg is the widow at Birka, one of the Svear and a Christian. Found at: Herigar's church. Rich, old and unbending: with no priest left in the town she keeps bought wine by her for three years, to be dropped in her mouth at the last. To look at: past seventy, upright in a chair, a fine dark gown with silver oval brooches and beads of glass and carnelian, a small cross among them, a sealed jar of wine on the shelf behind her.
pages.known: A real person. Born about 775. Rimbert, Vita Anskarii 20 (tr. Robinson 1921): the wine kept three years; 'there are here but few poor'. Her birth year is the game's guess (?). The book taken from the bishop's house is Rimbert 18 (from memory (?)).

later.text: Died in 852.
She died about 851-852, after Ardgar came.

pages.title: Catla
pages.hint: A pilgrim, not yet met
pages.brief: Catla, the pilgrim at Birka. Dutiful and practical: she does exactly what her mother asked, and when she and her helpers are weary she buys four pennies' worth of wine and goes on.
pages.game: Catla is the pilgrim at Birka, one of the Svear and a Christian. Found at: Herigar's church. Dutiful and practical: she does exactly what her mother asked, and when she and her helpers are weary she buys four pennies' worth of wine and goes on. To look at: about forty, sunburned, a plain travelling cloak over a good gown, her mother's beads, a heavy leather bag she carries herself and keeps on her lap.
pages.known: A real person. Rimbert, Vita Anskarii 20 (tr. Robinson 1921): 'There are there many churches, priests, and clergy, and a multitude of poor people'; the bag found full again but for the four pennies. The ties in Dorestad and Sliesthorp are invented.

pages.title: Holmsten
pages.hint: A merchant, not yet met
pages.brief: Holmsten, the merchant at Birka. Holmfast's grandson: the same scale case, the same two counts and a third weighing, but he has turned the house's trade east and wears a hammer and, since a voyage to Dorstadt, a small cross under it.
pages.game: Holmsten is the merchant at Birka, one of the Svear and one who keeps the old gods. Found at: the lanes of the Black Earth. Holmfast's grandson: the same scale case, the same two counts and a third weighing, but he has turned the house's trade east and wears a hammer and, since a voyage to Dorstadt, a small cross under it.
pages.known: Not in the record: the game's own person, set in a real place. 'Birka contained many rich merchants', and the Danes said each had more than the hundred pounds (Rimbert 19); men of Birka baptised at Dorstadt (Rimbert 27); hammer rings and crosses in the graves (Magnus 1999). Name: Holm- + -sten.
pages.source: Design/content/dossiers/birka.md (6 Oct 2026): the research this file is built on; its section 8 lists what must not be claimed.

later.text: In his thirties in the 850s, spare and pale-eyed like the old man, a short fair beard, a fur-edged cap and a belted eastern coat, the old round bronze scale case worn smooth, a hammer ring and a small cross on one cord inside his shirt.

pages.title: Vigmund of Birka
pages.hint: A warrior, not yet met
pages.brief: Vigmund, the warrior at Birka. A horseman of the hall below the fort who has ridden the eastern rivers and come back with a coat, a bow and a taste for board games.
pages.game: Vigmund is the warrior at Birka, one of the Svear and one who keeps the old gods. Found at: the fort rock. A horseman of the hall below the fort who has ridden the eastern rivers and come back with a coat, a bow and a taste for board games. To look at: a lean man with a clipped fair beard, a belted coat of eastern cut with a row of small bronze buttons and a silk band at the cuff, a fur-edged cap, a comb in a case at his belt and a leather bag of gaming pieces and dice.
pages.known: Not in the record: the game's own person, set in a real place. The coat with small bronze buttons is Geijer 1938 (?), the one place a button is right. Name: Vig- + -mund.
pages.source: Design/content/dossiers/birka.md (6 Oct 2026): the research this file is built on; its section 8 lists what must not be claimed.

pages.title: Seguin
pages.hint: A count, not yet met
pages.brief: Seguin, the count at Burdigala. A hard border lord who has held one river against one people for fifteen years and thinks that is the whole of the world.
pages.game: Seguin is the count at Burdigala, a Frank and a Christian. Found at: the count's enclosure. A hard border lord who has held one river against one people for fifteen years and thinks that is the whole of the world. To look at: about forty-five in 793, thick in the neck, cropped grey-brown hair, a long moustache and a shaved chin, a red tunic to the knee, a sword on a baldric and a hawking glove in his belt.
pages.known: A real person. Born about 750. Real: the count set over Bordeaux in 778 (the Astronomer, ch. 3). That he holds the city in 793 is not recorded (?).
pages.source: Design/content/dossiers/burdigala.md (4 Oct 2026): the research this file is built on; its section 8 lists what must not be claimed.

later.text: Real: the count set over Bordeaux in 778 (the Astronomer, ch. 3), probably the 'duke of the Gascons' deposed in 816 for arrogance and wicked ways.

pages.title: Amantius
pages.hint: A pilot, not yet met
pages.brief: Amantius, the pilot at Burdigala. Knows the river mouth the way a man knows his own stair in the dark, and is patient with those who do not.
pages.game: Amantius is the pilot at Burdigala, a Romance speaker and a Christian. Found at: the bank under the wall. Knows the river mouth the way a man knows his own stair in the dark, and is patient with those who do not. To look at: about forty-five in 793, lean and stooped, brown as a nut, white stubble, a short sleeveless cloak of goat hair, bare feet, a sounding pole taller than himself marked with rings of red cord.
pages.known: Not in the record: the game's own person, set in a real place. No shipman or pilot is named for Bordeaux. Amantius is a saint's name of the city (Saint Amand, 18 June), as Aquitanians bore Roman and saints' names. The estuary, its banks, width and bore: fr.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gironde_(estuaire); Blaye on the right bank: Gallia Christiana II. His miles are Roman miles: the estuary is up to 12 km wide, which is about eight of them.
pages.source: Design/content/dossiers/burdigala.md (4 Oct 2026): the research this file is built on; its section 8 lists what must not be claimed.

pages.title: Placidina
pages.hint: A widow, not yet met
pages.brief: Placidina, the widow at Burdigala. The last of a house that says it had senators in it: sells its wine by the cup with a straight back and forgets no slight in two hundred years.
pages.game: Placidina is the widow at Burdigala, a Romance speaker and a Christian. Found at: the house by the Broken Tower. The last of a house that says it had senators in it: sells its wine by the cup with a straight back and forgets no slight in two hundred years. To look at: about fifty in 793, small and upright, white hair under a dark veil, a long plain gown of good old cloth mended at the cuffs, a ring with a carved red stone, a bunch of iron keys.
pages.known: Not in the record: the game's own person, set in a real place. Placidina is an attested name of the city: the wife of Bishop Leontius II in the 6th century bore it (Venantius Fortunatus (?)); this ordinary widow shares only the name. The book is Ausonius's.
pages.source: Design/content/dossiers/burdigala.md (4 Oct 2026): the research this file is built on; its section 8 lists what must not be claimed.

pages.title: Bertric
pages.hint: A moneyer, not yet met
pages.brief: Bertric, the moneyer at Burdigala. A careful, cheerful man who trusts his scale and nothing else, and says so to counts.
pages.game: Bertric is the moneyer at Burdigala, a Frank and a Christian. Found at: the moneyer's bench. A careful, cheerful man who trusts his scale and nothing else, and says so to counts.
pages.known: Not in the record: the game's own person, set in a real place. No moneyer is named for Bordeaux. Bert- and -ric are Frankish name parts. The coins of Louis the Pious and Lothar I: Prou 1896; Melle as Aquitaine's silver; his death in the year the city fell is the game's.
pages.source: Design/content/dossiers/burdigala.md (4 Oct 2026): the research this file is built on; its section 8 lists what must not be claimed.

later.text: About thirty in 820, short and broad in the shoulder, a singed leather apron, a round felt cap, burn scars on both hands, a small hand balance on a cord round his neck.
Melle as Aquitaine's silver, sacked in 848: fr.wikipedia.org/wiki/Siège_de_Bordeaux_(847).

pages.title: Natan
pages.hint: A merchant, not yet met
pages.brief: Natan, the merchant at Burdigala. A dealer in wine, salt and whatever comes from Spain, who keeps his word because he cannot afford not to, and his temper for the same reason.
pages.game: Natan is the merchant at Burdigala, a Romance speaker and a Jew. Found at: the wine sellers by the old harbour. A dealer in wine, salt and whatever comes from Spain, who keeps his word because he cannot afford not to, and his temper for the same reason.
pages.known: Not in the record: the game's own person, set in a real place. Jews are named at Bordeaux once; no merchant of any people is named. The annal's charge of betrayal is one line by a distant bishop, and some read it as Pippin's party: it is never stated as fact. 'People' is set to romance because the peoples table has no row for him: see the report's needs.
pages.source: Design/content/dossiers/burdigala.md (4 Oct 2026): the research this file is built on; its section 8 lists what must not be claimed.

later.text: About forty in 840, tall and narrow, a trimmed black beard going grey, a long dark gown belted with a plain cord, a wax tablet at his belt, ink on his right thumb.
Jews are named at Bordeaux once, in 848 (Annales Bertiniani).

pages.title: Amalvinus
pages.hint: A count, not yet met
pages.brief: Amalvinus, the count at Burdigala. A count of a half-ruined city who has learned to be everybody's friend and to keep a fast horse.
pages.game: Amalvinus is the count at Burdigala, a Frank and a Christian. Found at: the count's enclosure. A count of a half-ruined city who has learned to be everybody's friend and to keep a fast horse.
pages.known: A real person. Real: Count Amalvinus of Bordeaux. His birth year, looks and manner are invented.
pages.source: Design/content/dossiers/burdigala.md (4 Oct 2026): the research this file is built on; its section 8 lists what must not be claimed.

later.text: Frotar's exile is Annales Bertiniani 876.
Real: Count Amalvinus of Bordeaux, at the council of Bourges in 887 and named in the letter of 906 as 'our friend'.
About forty in 890, tall and spare, fair hair gone thin, a short blue cloak pinned at the right shoulder, a sword with a silver-wired hilt, a letter folded small in his fist.

pages.title: Trencard
pages.hint: A lord's man, not yet met
pages.brief: Trencard, the lord's man at Burdigala. A young noble who can read, which makes him either the cleverest man in the hall or the oddest, depending on the hour.
pages.game: Trencard is the lord's man at Burdigala, a Romance speaker and a Christian. Found at: the count's enclosure. A young noble who can read, which makes him either the cleverest man in the hall or the oddest, depending on the hour.
pages.known: A real person. Real: Trencard, a young noble 'learned in letters', who answered Count William that old men remembered monks at the oratory of the Holy Cross, on his family's land, and gave it up. Nothing else is known of him: his dates, looks and later life are invented (?). The curse of Judas's lot and 100 pounds of gold is the charter's own.
pages.source: Design/content/dossiers/burdigala.md (4 Oct 2026): the research this file is built on; its section 8 lists what must not be claimed.

later.text: About twenty-five in 975, slight, dark hair cut straight across the brow, a green tunic with a woven border, a short sword he wears badly, a small book in a leather bag at his hip.

pages.title: Geoffrey
pages.hint: A bishop, not yet met
pages.brief: Geoffrey, the bishop at Burdigala. A Frank from the north set over Gascons and Aquitanians: honest, orderly, and aware that every one of them can hear it in his speech.
pages.game: Geoffrey is the bishop at Burdigala, a Frank and a Christian. Found at: Saint Andrew's, the bishop's church. A Frank from the north set over Gascons and Aquitanians: honest, orderly, and aware that every one of them can hear it in his speech.
pages.known: A real person. His birth year, looks and manner are invented.
pages.source: Design/content/dossiers/burdigala.md (4 Oct 2026): the research this file is built on; its section 8 lists what must not be claimed.

later.text: About forty-five in 1030, tall, clean-shaven and tonsured, a plain dark cope with one band of gold thread, a staff with a curled ivory head, a ring over his glove.
Real: Geoffrey II, 'a Frank by birth, honest in his ways', chosen and anointed at Blaye in 1027 before Duke Sancho's assembly, died 10 July 1043, buried at Saint Seurin.
Died in 1043.

pages.title: Felix
pages.hint: A merchant, not yet met
pages.brief: Felix, the merchant at Burdigala. Sells the oil that comes up from the south by river and cart: a soft-spoken man with a long memory for debts and a longer one for who paid early.
pages.game: Felix is the merchant at Burdigala, a Romance speaker and a Christian. Found at: the wine sellers by the old harbour. Sells the oil that comes up from the south by river and cart: a soft-spoken man with a long memory for debts and a longer one for who paid early. To look at: about forty-five, plump, oiled grey hair, a long undyed linen tunic with stained cuffs, a dipping rod and a string of little tasting spoons at his belt.
pages.known: Not in the record: the game's own person, set in a real place. The Bordeaux oil ship and the forty measures are in the Life of Saint Philibert. No oil seller of Bordeaux is named in any source.
pages.source: Design/content/dossiers/burdigala.md (4 Oct 2026): the research this file is built on; its section 8 lists what must not be claimed.

pages.title: Hildebold
pages.hint: A bishop, not yet met
pages.brief: Hildebold, the bishop at Colonia. The king's archchaplain: a court man, quick, well read, used to being obeyed without raising his voice.
pages.game: Hildebold is the bishop at Colonia, a Frank and a Christian. Found at: Saint Peter's. The king's archchaplain: a court man, quick, well read, used to being obeyed without raising his voice. Home at Colonia only for the great feasts. To look at: about fifty, lean, clean-shaven, a tonsure gone grey; a plain dark wool cloak over a long white tunic, a gold ring, and a small prayer book bound in deer hide in his hand.
pages.known: A real person. Bishop 787, archchaplain 791, archbishop 794/795. His birth year is not known. The deer-hide tale is a late legend, turned round here on purpose.
pages.source: Design/content/dossiers/colonia.md (4 October 2026), which this file follows; its own references are repeated here where used.

later.text: The church he had about 800 burned some ten years later: so he speaks of fire as a fear and of building as an intention, in any year.
His court name Aaron and his consecration of Liudger at Colonia on 30 March 805 are in the same article (checked 7 October 2026).
Bishop 787, archchaplain 791, archbishop 794/795, died 3 September 818.
Died in 818.

pages.title: Hrotbert
pages.hint: A clerk, not yet met
pages.brief: Hrotbert, the clerk at Colonia. The bishop's clerk for the mint, the gate and the king's lists: exact, tireless, fond of a rule he can read aloud.
pages.game: Hrotbert is the clerk at Colonia, a Frank and a Christian. Found at: the river gate and the king's mint. The bishop's clerk for the mint, the gate and the king's lists: exact, tireless, fond of a rule he can read aloud. To look at: about thirty, thin and stooped, ink on the right thumb, a clerk's tonsure; a grey tunic to the shin, a wax tablet and stylus hung at his belt, a ring of keys.
pages.known: Not in the record: the game's own person, set in a real place.
pages.source: Design/content/dossiers/colonia.md (4 October 2026), which this file follows; its own references are repeated here where used.

later.text: The rule he reads is Frankfurt 794 c. 5; the wheat price is Frankfurt 794 c. 4.

pages.title: Erkanbert
pages.hint: A priest, not yet met
pages.brief: Erkanbert, the priest at Colonia. The old priest of the river strip and the graves outside the wall: blunt, tired, kind in a way that costs him.
pages.game: Erkanbert is the priest at Colonia, a Frank and a Christian. Found at: the Deutz crossing and the Golden Saints. The old priest of the river strip and the graves outside the wall: blunt, tired, kind in a way that costs him. To look at: near sixty, broad and red-faced, a white fringe round a bald crown; a patched brown cloak, muddy shoes, a wooden cross on a thong and a satchel with a book in it.
pages.known: Not in the record: the game's own person, set in a real place. The vow is the Old Saxon baptismal vow. Gereon and the soldiers of the Theban Legion: de.wikipedia St. Gereon.
pages.source: Design/content/dossiers/colonia.md (4 October 2026), which this file follows; its own references are repeated here where used.

pages.title: Meginher
pages.hint: A merchant, not yet met
pages.brief: Meginher, a merchant at Colonia. A dealer in querns and millstones from the Mayen pits: patient, heavy, thinks in boatloads and years.
pages.game: Meginher is a merchant at Colonia, a Frank and a Christian. Found at: the market on the old harbour ground. A dealer in querns and millstones from the Mayen pits: patient, heavy, thinks in boatloads and years. To look at: mid-forties, thick-armed and grey with stone dust to the elbows, a full brown beard; a leather apron over a russet tunic, a measuring stick notched in hand-breadths.
pages.known: Not in the record: the game's own person, set in a real place. Mayen lava querns down the Rhine and finished at Dorestad. That the stones were querns is one reading of it (?).
pages.source: Design/content/dossiers/colonia.md (4 October 2026), which this file follows; its own references are repeated here where used.

later.text: The black stones and the cloaks are in Charles's letter to Offa of 796.

pages.title: Gerhild
pages.hint: A widow, not yet met
pages.brief: Gerhild, the widow at Colonia. A potter's widow from the Vorgebirge who sells the villages' jars by the stack and fills them with wine for the north: sharp, funny, never short-measured.
pages.game: Gerhild is the widow at Colonia, a Frank and a Christian. Found at: the market on the old harbour ground. A potter's widow from the Vorgebirge who sells the villages' jars by the stack and fills them with wine for the north: sharp, funny, never short-measured. To look at: about forty, small and wiry, sleeves rolled, clay under the nails; a head cloth, a madder-red dress kilted up for work, a tasting cup on a cord at her waist.
pages.known: Not in the record: the game's own person, set in a real place. Women trading in their own names are not attested (?), a potter's widow selling for the kiln is the game's. Badorf ware from Walberberg, Eckdorf and Badorf with Colonia its market and loading place. The tin-foil jugs are Tating ware, found from Dorestad to Birka.
pages.source: Design/content/dossiers/colonia.md (4 October 2026), which this file follows; its own references are repeated here where used.

pages.title: Wido of Colonia
pages.hint: A steward, not yet met
pages.brief: Wido, the steward at Colonia. Steward of the king's estate at Deutz: loud, honest in the king's interest, short of boats every year of his life.
pages.game: Wido is the steward at Colonia, a Frank and a Christian. Found at: the strand under the wall and the Deutz crossing. Steward of the king's estate at Deutz: loud, honest in the king's interest, short of boats every year of his life. To look at: early forties, big-bellied and sunburnt, cropped fair hair and a long moustache; a good blue cloak with a silver pin, riding boots, a bundle of split tally sticks.
pages.known: Not in the record: the game's own person, set in a real place. Deutz as a royal estate: de.wikipedia Kastell Deutz.
pages.source: Design/content/dossiers/colonia.md (4 October 2026), which this file follows; its own references are repeated here where used.

later.text: The king's own grain sold below the top price: Synod of Frankfurt 794 c. 4.

pages.title: Bero
pages.hint: A smith, not yet met
pages.brief: Bero, the smith at Colonia. A blade smith who deals in other smiths' work as well as his own.
pages.game: Bero is the smith at Colonia, a Frank and a Christian. Found at: the smiths' row. A blade smith who deals in other smiths' work as well as his own. Careful, incurious by policy, proud of his welds. To look at: about forty, spare and burn-scarred on the forearms, dark hair tied back, singed eyebrows; a leather apron, bare arms, a folding balance in a wooden case in his shirt.
pages.known: Not in the record: the game's own person, set in a real place. Sword with scabbard at 7 solidi: Lex Ribuaria 40 (36) c. 11. The ban: Herstal 779 c. 20. The name welded into blades is the Ulfberht mark, 9th to 11th century, with many imitations.
pages.source: Design/content/dossiers/colonia.md (4 October 2026), which this file follows; its own references are repeated here where used.

later.text: The capitulary for the missi of 803.
Thionville 805 c. 7.

pages.title: Adaltrud
pages.hint: An alewife, not yet met
pages.brief: Adaltrud, the alewife at Colonia. Keeps the ale-house in the wall tower: remembers every face and every debt, and is the one person on the strand who is told everything.
pages.game: Adaltrud is the alewife at Colonia, a Frank and a Christian. Found at: the ale-house in the tower. Keeps the ale-house in the wall tower: remembers every face and every debt, and is the one person on the strand who is told everything. To look at: early thirties, tall and strong-armed, a broad calm face, fair plaits under a linen head cloth; an undyed apron over a green dress, a ladle, a bunch of tally sticks on a nail behind her.
pages.known: Not in the record: the game's own person, set in a real place. The house is the game's (?). After her the house is kept by her daughter Hiltrud and Hiltrud's children, who keep the chipped cup for the merchant's heirs.
pages.source: Design/content/dossiers/colonia.md (4 October 2026), which this file follows; its own references are repeated here where used.

pages.title: Liutwin
pages.hint: A merchant, not yet met
pages.brief: Liutwin, a merchant at Colonia. Head of a house that sells Rhenish wine by the cask and the green glass to drink it from: smooth, exact, never seen to hurry, and never seen to carry anything himself.
pages.game: Liutwin is a merchant at Colonia, a Frank and a Christian. Found at: the market on the old harbour ground. Head of a house that sells Rhenish wine by the cask and the green glass to drink it from: smooth, exact, never seen to hurry, and never seen to carry anything himself. To look at: about forty-five, tall and narrow, a trimmed grey-brown beard, a long tunic of good dark red wool, clean hands, a small green glass beaker hung in a net at his belt.
pages.known: Not in the record: the game's own person, set in a real place. Rhenish wine in casks from Colonia to Dorestad and the palaces; glass working on the river strip (the Heumarkt dig (?)); glass beakers from the Rhine found from Dorestad to Birka.
pages.source: Design/content/dossiers/colonia.md (4 October 2026), which this file follows; its own references are repeated here where used.

later.text: After 817 the house goes on under his sons.

pages.title: Hadebald
pages.hint: A bishop, not yet met
pages.brief: Hadebald, the bishop at Colonia. Archbishop after Hildebold: a builder and a lender of books, more often in his city than his master was, and generous with what the church can spare, boats included.
pages.game: Hadebald is the bishop at Colonia, a Frank and a Christian. Found at: Saint Peter's. Archbishop after Hildebold: a builder and a lender of books, more often in his city than his master was, and generous with what the church can spare, boats included.
pages.known: A real person. His birth year is not known (0). His looks, his character and his words are invented; whether he and Einhard dealt with each other is not recorded (?).
pages.source: Design/content/dossiers/colonia.md (4 October 2026), which this file follows; its own references are repeated here where used.

later.text: About fifty in 826, broad and ruddy, a grey tonsure, a good brown travelling cloak over white, a mason's cord and a book list on one thong at his belt.
Died in 841.
Hadebald, archbishop of Colonia 819 to 841; the boat with two cabins given to Harald and Anskar in 826: Rimbert, Vita Anskarii c. 7 (tr. Robinson 1921); the 175 books listed in 833.

pages.title: Bruno
pages.hint: A bishop, not yet met
pages.brief: Bruno, the bishop at Colonia. King Otto's youngest brother, archbishop and duke of Lotharingia at once: learned, sleepless, a man who reads on horseback and rules a town between two chapters.
pages.game: Bruno is the bishop at Colonia, a Saxon and a Christian. Found at: Saint Peter's and Saint Martin's on the island. King Otto's youngest brother, archbishop and duke of Lotharingia at once: learned, sleepless, a man who reads on horseback and rules a town between two chapters. To look at: about thirty, slight and pale, short fair hair under a plain cap, a dark wool cloak with no gold on it but the ring, a book in a saddle bag and ink on his cuff.
pages.known: A real person. From his day the archbishop held court, market, mint and toll. That he had Greek is Ruotger's Life, from memory (?). His looks and words are invented.
pages.source: Design/content/dossiers/colonia.md (4 October 2026), which this file follows; its own references are repeated here where used.

later.text: Bruno (Brun), born 925, King Otto I's brother.
Archbishop of Colonia and duke of Lotharingia from 953.
The Lech, 955: chronicle.
A chapter at Saint Martin's about 960 and an abbey at Saint Pantaleon.
Died at Reims on 11 October 965.
Died in 965.

pages.title: Brunger
pages.hint: A mate, not yet met
pages.brief: Brunger, the mate at Daventre. Strong, loyal to the boat, slow to speak and slower to forgive; said the baptismal vow because the law is baptism or death.
pages.game: Brunger is the mate at Daventre, a Saxon and a Christian. Found at: the bank below the church and Hathugard's ale-house. Strong, loyal to the boat, slow to speak and slower to forgive; said the baptismal vow because the law is baptism or death. To look at: late twenties, tall and heavy in the shoulder, long fair hair, a moustache and no beard; an undyed tunic, a long knife (a seax) across his belly.
pages.known: Not in the record: the game's own person, set in a real place. The brother's name Brunric (Brun- + -ric, the family stem) is this file's and should be made to agree with whoever writes Mogontia.

pages.known: Not in the record: the game's own person, set in a real place. Name of two attested Saxon parts, Hathu- and -gard.

pages.title: Liudbod
pages.hint: A priest, not yet met
pages.brief: Liudbod, the priest at Daventre. Patient and practical: a schoolboy of Utrecht who carried planks when the church was built the third time and has kept it standing since.
pages.game: Liudbod is the priest at Daventre, a Frisian and a Christian. Found at: Lebuin's church. pages.title: Einbert
pages.hint: A smith, not yet met
pages.brief: Einbert, the smith at Daventre. Proud of heath iron and of the king, in that order; judges a man by his hands.
pages.game: Einbert is the smith at Daventre, a Frank and a Christian. Found at: the forge on the bank. Proud of heath iron and of the king, in that order; judges a man by his hands. To look at: about forty, broad, short brown hair singed at the front, a long moustache, a leather apron over a bare chest, burn scars on both forearms, tongs in his fist.
pages.known: Not in the record: the game's own person, set in a real place. Name of two attested Frankish parts, Ein- and -bert.

pages.title: Thancric
pages.hint: A ferryman, not yet met
pages.brief: Thancric, the ferryman at Daventre. Counts everything that crosses and takes no side out loud; has carried saints' men, hostages and armies over the same water for the same fare.

Given Duisburg and Kaiserswerth after 1016 or about 1011.
Founded Brauweiler in 1024.
The election at Kamba, 1024.
Married Matilda, daughter of Otto II (died 1025).

pages.title: Adelsuit
pages.hint: A farm wife, not yet met
pages.brief: Adelsuit, the farm wife at Doccinga. Certain. She has told one story all her life and has never changed a word of it that she will admit to.
pages.game: Adelsuit is the farm wife at Doccinga, a Frisian and a Christian. Found at: the spring on the mound and the meadow and the reeds. Certain. She has told one story all her life and has never changed a word of it that she will admit to. To look at: in 793 about fifty, broad, weather-brown, a grey head-cloth and an undyed gown, a yoke and two buckets.
pages.known: A real person. Born about 744. A very old woman who swore, to a cleric of Utrecht in the first half of the 9th century, that she saw Boniface cover his head with a gospel book: the Utrecht Life, in Levison's edition p. 73, as in Robinson's note. She is real and has no name in the source: the name Adelsuit (Adel- + -suit), her birth year and her kin are ours (?).

The oak weaving sword and the pin with inlaid stones are finds from Aalsum; 'the woman who makes fresum' and the higher fine for her hand: Lex Frisionum, judgements of Wlemar. The Frisian cloaks white, grey, red and blue sent to the caliph: Notker II.9 (tr. Grant 1907), paraphrased.

pages.game: Cynehelm is the priest at Dofras, one of the English and a Christian. Found at: the two tallies, at the old south gate and Saint Martin's, the wooden minster. The canon who keeps Saint Martin's half of the toll and its three books, and is prouder of the tally than he thinks a priest should be. The canons as secular clerks 'subject to no one except the court of Rome and the king', their half of the toll and their common fund: Victoria County History, Kent, vol. 2. Wihtred's law on the stranger: Wikipedia (en) 'Law of Wihtred' (our wording). Saint Martin's cloak: Sulpicius Severus, Vita Martini 3.

pages.title: Hildgyth
pages.hint: A weaver, not yet met
pages.brief: Hildgyth, the weaver at Dofras. The best weaver under the west wall, with six looms and four daughters, and a memory for every cloak she ever sold and to whom.
pages.game: Hildgyth is the weaver at Dofras, one of the English and a Christian. Found at: the trodden ground before Saint Martin's and the weaving huts under the west wall. The best weaver under the west wall, with six looms and four daughters, and a memory for every cloak she ever sold and to whom. The black merchant is Alcuin's Hrotberct (carmen 4). A host answers for a guest: the Kentish law of Hlothhere and Eadric c. 15, used here by likeness (?). 'A farthing' is a quarter of a penny by cutting (?).

pages.title: Rorik
pages.hint: A count, not yet met
pages.brief: Rorik, the count at Dorestat. A sea-raider made a count: keeps his oath for as long as it keeps him, and keeps other raiders off the river better than the emperor could.

Died in 880.
He held the vicus with his brother Harald under Louis, took it in 850, and is dead by 882.

pages.title: Hrotberct
pages.hint: A merchant, not yet met
pages.brief: Hrotberct, the merchant at Dorestat. The black-haired merchant of the bank: rich, close, quick with a price, and famous on the river for never having lodged a guest.
pages.game: Hrotberct is the merchant at Dorestat, a Frank and a Christian. Found at: the row behind the bank road. The black-haired merchant of the bank: rich, close, quick with a price, and famous on the river for never having lodged a guest. To look at: about fifty, lean, black hair going grey at the temples, a sharp shaved chin, a good dark tunic with no ornament at all, a covered balance always under his hand.
pages.known: A real person. Born about 740. Historical in name only: 'niger Hrotberct', the 'mercator avarus' of Dorestad who will give the traveller no lodging, in Alcuin's carmen 4, lines 9-11 (MGH Poetae I, pp. 220-223), written before 782. That he was alive in 793, that he sold wax, and everything he says are invented (?).

pages.title: Aldgard

pages.brief: Aldgard, the alewife at Dorestat. Aldswith's granddaughter, who keeps the old house on the bank road in the Dane's years: pours for four tongues, gives to the church without counting, and counts everything else.

later.text: About twenty-five in 850: strong, grey-eyed, a linen head-cloth, a dark apron-dress pinned with two old bronze brooches that were her grandmother's, a wine jug in her hand as often as an ale ladle.

pages.hint: A monk, not yet met
pages.brief: Óengus, the monk at Duiblinn. Máel Ruain's pupil, a client of God at Tallaght, making a calendar in verse with a saint for every day of the year: exact, dry, and kinder than his rule.
pages.game: Óengus is the monk at Duiblinn, one of the Irish and a Christian. Found at: Máel Ruain's house at Tallaght. Máel Ruain's pupil, a client of God at Tallaght, making a calendar in verse with a saint for every day of the year: exact, dry, and kinder than his rule. To look at: about forty-five in 793, lean, the tonsure grown grey at the edges, a patched undyed habit with the hood back, ink on two fingers, a wax tablet tied to his belt with a thong.
pages.known: A real person. Born about 750. Real: Óengus son of Óengoba, the Culdee, pupil of Máel Ruain at Tallaght. That he questioned a merchant for saints' days is invented. The ale: The Monastery of Tallaght 6 (Gwynn and Purton 1911), retold. The saying: 'To go to Rome', Kuno Meyer, Selections from Ancient Irish Poetry (1911), retold in prose. The ink: scribes' margins, Thesaurus Palaeohibernicus II (1903).

Struck the first pennies about 995 to 997.
About thirty in 1000, slight, a fine fair beard combed and oiled, a red silk cap and a cloak edged with marten, a short sword in a gilt scabbard, a new penny turned over and over in his fingers.
Stayed inside at Clontarf in 1014.
Went to Rome in 1028.
His son's ransom in 1029.

pages.title: Amlaíb Cuarán
pages.hint: A king, not yet met
pages.brief: Amlaíb Cuarán, the king at Duiblinn. King of the foreigners of Dublin for most of forty years, and twice king at York before the English put him out: shrewd, amused, baptised with a king for godfather.
pages.game: Amlaíb Cuarán is the king at Duiblinn, one of the Northmen and a Christian. Found at: the king's hall. King of the foreigners of Dublin for most of forty years, and twice king at York before the English put him out: shrewd, amused, baptised with a king for godfather. To look at: past fifty and looking seventy, big-framed and gone gaunt, white beard cut short, a penitent's coarse grey tunic with the mark of arm-rings still pale on his wrists, one plain sandal mended with cord.
pages.known: A real person. He was not at Tara himself. 'Cuaran' means sandal. His birth year is a guess (?). The Dublin lines are invented.

later.text: In 980, after his sons lose at Tara, an old man who gives it all up and goes to Colum Cille's island a penitent, and finds he is curious about his own soul.
He is placed at Dublin, where he was king from 945 to 947 and from 952 to 980, and is met on Hi only in his last year.
Died in 981.
Annals of Tigernach 980; en.wikipedia Amlaib Cuaran: king at York about 941-944 and 949-952, baptised 943 with King Edmund as sponsor (Anglo-Saxon Chronicle 943), died on Hi in 980 or 981.

pages.title: Cerball
pages.hint: A king, not yet met
pages.brief: Cerball, the king at Duiblinn.
pages.game: Cerball is the king at Duiblinn, one of the Irish and a Christian. Found at: the black pool. King of Leinster, who with the king of Brega drove the foreigners out of the fort and left their ships half built on the strand: vigorous, proud, a friend to poets, and not sure what to do with an empty harbour. To look at: about forty, big, red-bearded, a many-coloured cloak with a gold brooch the width of a hand, a sword with an ivory hilt that he likes to be asked about, poets and hounds at his heels.
pages.known: A real person. Cerball son of Muirecán, king of Leinster. His birth year is a guess; that a merchant met him at the empty pool, his looks and his words are invented.

Died in 909.
Cerball son of Muirecán, king of Leinster, died 909 (Annals of Ulster 909 (?)).

later.text: Grandson of Ímar, called the One-eyed: took the pool back with a fleet in 917, killed a king of Tara outside it, and already has his good eye on York.
Died in 927.

Sitriuc grandson of Ímar, called Cáech ('one-eyed' or 'squinting'): retook Dublin in 917, defeated and killed Niall Glúndub, king of Tara, outside it in 919, left for York in 920, was king there from 921, married a sister of King Æthelstan in 926 and died in 927.

pages.brief: Bernlef, the singer at Emuthon. Loved by his neighbours because he is courteous and knows the deeds of the men of old and the wars of kings by heart; kept the secret of his healing as he was told.
pages.game: Bernlef is the singer at Emuthon, a Frisian and a Christian. Found at: the house with the looms and the crossing to the Nesse. Loved by his neighbours because he is courteous and knows the deeds of the men of old and the wars of kings by heart; kept the secret of his healing as he was told. To look at: about sixty, big-framed and gentle, white hair to the shoulder, eyes that look a little past you from habit, a blue-grey cloak, a stick he no longer needs; his wife leads him by the sleeve out of long use.
pages.known: A real person. Born about 733. Altfrid, Vita Liudgeri I.25-26 (ed. Diekamp 1881): blind three years, healed by Liudger, sang the deeds of the men of old and the wars of kings, baptised eighteen dying infants in the rising, learned the psalms. He lived at Helewyret (Holwierde) across the Ems mouth and is not recorded at Emden; his birth year is a guess and his death year is not known (?). Finn Folcwalding: Widsith and Beowulf.

pages.title: Alcuin
pages.hint: An abbot, not yet met
pages.brief: Alcuin, the abbot at Eoforwic. The best teacher of his age and a tireless writer of letters: homesick for York's books, fond of riddles and pet names, scolds kings and bishops alike.
pages.game: Alcuin is the abbot at Eoforwic, one of the English and a Christian. Alcuin is deacon of York; master at the king's court. Found at: Saint Peter's minster. The best teacher of his age and a tireless writer of letters: homesick for York's books, fond of riddles and pet names, scolds kings and bishops alike. To look at: nearing sixty, slight, tonsured grey, a deacon's plain dark dress, ink on his fingers, a pile of wax tablets and a boy to carry them; never seen without a book. Temper at the start: grieving. That is: slow to act, generous to the church, easier to move by Troth and harder by Tongue.
pages.known: A real person. Born about 735. He is not at York in person in the game's years. Every line is our own rendering or paraphrase of his letters (MGH Epistolae IV nos. 20, 121, 232 (?)) and of the Disputatio Pippini, never a printed translation. Born about 735. Why that temper: from June 793 he writes of nothing but Northumbria: the blood on the altar, the sins that earned it.

pages.known: A real person. Ealdorman Alfred and his wife Wærburh, who bought the gold-lettered gospel book 'from the heathen army' with pure gold and gave it to Christ Church: the Old English note in the Stockholm Codex Aureus, which names their daughter and a goldsmith Wulfhelm. His will survives; his years here (865-888), his birth, his manner and his words are ours (?).

To look at: about thirty, stooped from the block, cropped brown hair, a smith's forearms; a dark tunic of good cloth gone shiny at the knees, a bunch of die-keys, a small silver cross.
pages.known: A real person. Leofsige signs pennies of Æthelred II at GIPES (Hildebrand, Anglosachsiska mynt, 1881; read from a rough scan (?)). His years, face and words are the game's. The ealdorman's answer: The Battle of Maldon.
pages.source: Design/content/dossiers/gipeswic.md (the research this file is built on; its section 8 lists what must not be claimed)

later.text: Died in 1018.

pages.title: Botgair
pages.hint: A merchant, not yet met
pages.brief: Botgair, a merchant at Grobiņa. The oldest of the Gotland traders on the black earth, born here like his father.
pages.game: Botgair is a merchant at Grobiņa, a Gotlander and one who keeps the old gods. Found at: the black earth, the Gotlanders' store and Rodlikn's long house. The oldest of the Gotland traders on the black earth, born here like his father. Patient, exact, and fonder of this place than of the island he calls home and has seen four times. To look at: near fifty, lean, grey-fair beard in a single plait, a brown wool tunic to the knee with a tablet-woven hem, a Gotland belt buckle of bronze, a folding balance in a wooden case hung at his hip.
pages.known: Not in the record: the game's own person, set in a real place. Gotlanders living and buried here are from the grave fields; no trader of the place is named. Name: Bót- + -gair, both on the later rune stones of Gotland (?).
pages.source: Design/content/dossiers/grobin.md (6 Oct 2026): the research this file is built on, with what could and could not be checked.

pages.title: Rodlikn
pages.hint: A widow, not yet met
pages.brief: Rodlikn, the widow at Grobiņa. A Gotland widow who keeps the long house where strangers sleep.
pages.game: Rodlikn is the widow at Grobiņa, a Gotlander and one who keeps the old gods. Found at: the women's ground and Rodlikn's long house. A Gotland widow who keeps the long house where strangers sleep. Remembers every crew by where they sat, what they drank and what they left unpaid, and holds none of it against them. To look at: about forty, small and straight, fair hair under a linen cloth, a dark wool dress held by two animal-head brooches of Gotland make with a string of glass beads between, a box brooch at the throat, keys and a small knife on a chain.
pages.known: Not in the record: the game's own person, set in a real place. Women in the flat graves wear Gotland's own brooches and buckles; the animal-head and box brooches are Gotland's kinds (from memory (?)). No woman of the place is named. Name: Hróð- + -líkn, both on Gotland's stones (?).
pages.source: Design/content/dossiers/grobin.md (6 Oct 2026): the research this file is built on, with what could and could not be checked.

pages.title: Arnvald
pages.hint: A warrior, not yet met
pages.brief: Arnvald, the warrior at Grobiņa. The head of the few armed Svear who still sit on the fort hill, as their fathers did.
pages.game: Arnvald is the warrior at Grobiņa, one of the Svear and one who keeps the old gods. Found at: the gate of the fort and the field of the armed men. The head of the few armed Svear who still sit on the fort hill, as their fathers did. Proud, bored, and honest enough to know that eleven men are not a lordship. To look at: mid-thirties, broad, red-brown beard cut square, a grey wool tunic and wide trousers bound at the calf, a single-edged long knife in a worn scabbard across the belly, a shield with an iron boss leaning by him.
pages.known: Not in the record: the game's own person, set in a real place. One of the three grave fields is 'military in character', with men of the Mälar valley under low mounds with their weapons; the Cori 'had in former time been in subjection to the Swedes, but had a long while since rebelled' (Rimbert c. 30, Robinson 1921). That a few Svear still sat on the fort in 793 is the game's reading of an open question (?); he is no ruler and is called none. Name: Arn- + -vald, both on the Uppland stones.
pages.source: Design/content/dossiers/grobin.md (6 Oct 2026): the research this file is built on, with what could and could not be checked.

pages.title: Kantegede
pages.hint: An interpreter, not yet met
pages.brief: Kantegede, the interpreter at Grobiņa. The Curonian who stands between the hill forts inland and the strangers' booths: three tongues, a long memory, and a habit of agreeing with the last speaker until the weighing starts.
pages.game: Kantegede is the interpreter at Grobiņa, a Prussian or a Curonian and of the faith called baltic gods. Found at: the bank under the hill and the black earth. The Curonian who stands between the hill forts inland and the strangers' booths: three tongues, a long memory, and a habit of agreeing with the last speaker until the weighing starts. To look at: about forty-five, tall, clean chin and long fair moustache, a pale undyed wool tunic with a bronze neck ring and a spiral arm ring, a staff notched along one side, soft hide shoes.
pages.known: Not in the record: the game's own person, set in a real place. No Curonian of these years is named in any source; a go-between is inferred from two peoples trading in one place, and he is no chief. Neck and arm rings of bronze as Baltic dress are from memory (?). Name: two Old Prussian stems of the later records standing in, since no Curonian name survives before 1230 (?).
pages.source: Design/content/dossiers/grobin.md (6 Oct 2026): the research this file is built on, with what could and could not be checked.

pages.title: Wissegerde
pages.hint: A merchant, not yet met
pages.brief: Wissegerde, a merchant at Grobiņa. Kantegede's son, a boy at the plank in 793 and the man who runs the market for the Curonians once the hill is theirs.
pages.game: Wissegerde is a merchant at Grobiņa, a Prussian or a Curonian and of the faith called baltic gods. Found at: the bank under the hill, the black earth and the gate of the fort. Kantegede's son, a boy at the plank in 793 and the man who runs the market for the Curonians once the hill is theirs. Sharper than his father and less polite; he learned to count from strangers and has not forgiven them for it.
pages.known: Not in the record: the game's own person, set in a real place. The Danes' defeat and the gold and ships taken from them are Rimbert c. 30 (Robinson 1921). A truce counted in days is the saga's picture of a Kurland market. He dies in the burning unless the house got him out (the story 'The gods who would not answer'). Name: Wisse- and -gerde, Old Prussian stems of the later records standing in (?).
pages.source: Design/content/dossiers/grobin.md (6 Oct 2026): the research this file is built on, with what could and could not be checked.

later.text: A young man in 800 and grey by 850: tall like his father, fair hair tied back, a blue-dyed tunic with a bronze neck ring, a folding balance of the Northmen's kind at his belt and a spear never far off.
That the Curonians take the place over between 800 and 850 is the Latvian pages' account.

pages.title: Tulegaud
pages.hint: A pilot, not yet met
pages.brief: Tulegaud, the pilot at Grobiņa. The Curonian who takes ships over the bar and across the lake.
pages.game: Tulegaud is the pilot at Grobiņa, a Prussian or a Curonian and of the faith called baltic gods. Found at: the bar and the open shore, the reed lake and Rodlikn's long house. The Curonian who takes ships over the bar and across the lake. Cheerful, incurious about cargoes, and never wrong about water he has poled that morning. To look at: under thirty, wiry and burnt brown, fair hair cropped with a knife, a short sleeveless hide coat over a wool shirt, bare legs wet to the thigh, a sounding pole twice his height marked in hand-spans.
pages.known: Not in the record: the game's own person, set in a real place. The outlet from the lake kept silting shut and shifting until the canal of 1697-1703: a place like that has a man who knows this morning's water. Where the outlet lay and how deep it was in 793 are unknown, and he names no mark. Name: Tule- and -gaud, Old Prussian stems of the later records standing in (?).
pages.source: Design/content/dossiers/grobin.md (6 Oct 2026): the research this file is built on, with what could and could not be checked.

pages.title: Buite
pages.hint: A wise woman, not yet met
pages.brief: Buite, the wise woman at Grobiņa. The old Curonian woman who is asked.
pages.game: Buite is the wise woman at Grobiņa, a Prussian or a Curonian and of the faith called baltic gods. Found at: the house of the woman who is asked. The old Curonian woman who is asked. Says little, sees who is lying, and treats a Northman's fever and a Curonian's the same, at the same price. To look at: near sixty, bent, white hair in two plaits under a wool cloth, a dark dress pinned at the shoulders with bronze pins joined by a chain, a string of rough amber, hands stained green and brown.
pages.known: Not in the record: the game's own person, set in a real place. Adam of Bremen, about 1075: the Curonians' houses are 'full of pagan soothsayers, diviners and necromancers': late, and used lightly. No god, rite or Curonian word is named, because none is recorded for these years. Pins joined by a chain as Baltic women's dress are from memory (?). Name: Buite, a Prussian woman's name of the 13th to 15th century records, standing in (?).
pages.source: Design/content/dossiers/grobin.md (6 Oct 2026): the research this file is built on, with what could and could not be checked.

pages.title: Vigfast
pages.hint: A merchant, not yet met
pages.brief: Vigfast, a merchant at Grobiņa. A Birka fur trader who comes here by the Curonians' leave in the last years, and who has stood at the back of the priest's house at Birka often enough to be unsure which gods he owes.
pages.game: Vigfast is a merchant at Grobiņa, one of the Svear and one who keeps the old gods. Found at: the black earth. A Birka fur trader who comes here by the Curonians' leave in the last years, and who has stood at the back of the priest's house at Birka often enough to be unsure which gods he owes. To look at: about thirty-five, stocky, fair beard trimmed close, a good red-brown cloak with a ring pin of silver, wide trousers, a small hammer of iron on a thong at his neck and a cross of the same size beside it.
pages.known: Not in the record: the game's own person, set in a real place. To stand for the unnamed Svea merchants in Olof's host who 'had heard' Anskar and advised asking Christ, and for the vow kept afterwards: seven days at home, seven without meat, and after forty days another forty. The lots at Birka about Anskar's coming: Rimbert c. 26-27 (?). His last two rumours are said only after the war, at Birka. Name: Víg- + -fast, both on the Uppland stones.

pages.hint: An abbot, not yet met
pages.brief: Friduin, the abbot at Gyrwe. A careful, tired man who rules two houses ten miles apart and has read Alcuin's letter more often than he will say.
pages.game: Friduin is the abbot at Gyrwe, one of the English and a Christian. Found at: Saint Paul's and the abbot's hall and the refectory. A careful, tired man who rules two houses ten miles apart and has read Alcuin's letter more often than he will say. To look at: fifties, lean, grey tonsure, a plain undyed cowl darned at the elbow, a small bronze key and a wax tablet on his girdle, an abbot's staff of ash with no gold on it.
pages.known: A real person. Born about 740. Friduin (Frithuwine), abbot of Wearmouth and Jarrow: Alcuin wrote to him on his election; Victoria County History, Durham, vol. 2; Jaffe, Monumenta Alcuiniana. Every line is invented.

pages.brief: Elfred son of Westou, the priest at Gyrwe. Priest and sacrist of Durham, keeper of Saint Cuthbert's body, and a tireless collector of other saints: quiet, devout, and never seen leaving with anything.
pages.game: Elfred son of Westou is the priest at Gyrwe, one of the English and a Christian. Found at: Saint Paul's. later.text: Elfred (Alfred) son of Westou, sacrist of Durham under bishops Edmund, Aethelric and Aethelwine, about 1020 to after 1056: Symeon of Durham, History of the Church of Durham (tr. Stevenson 1855): he came yearly for Bede's day, left early and alone one year, never came again, and 'conducted himself like a person who had secured the object of his desires'.
Died in 1060.

The whale-vertebra block, the fish-scratched comb, the green turtle bone and the mounds built over are finds (Morton 1992; Garner 1993; Ellis and Andrews 2006). pages.game: Ceolhelm is the priest at Hamwic, one of the English and a Christian. Found at: the shore church and St Mary's above the hythe. The priest of the shore church, schooled at Nursling where Boniface taught: a careful man with a head full of Aldhelm's riddles and a parish full of sailors. To look at: about forty-eight, thin and stooped, tonsured grey hair, a plain undyed gown and a dark cloak pinned with bone, ink on his right thumb, a wax tablet tied to his girdle.
pages.known: Not in the record: the game's own person, set in a real place. Ceol- and -helm are English name parts. Nursling, six km off, was Boniface's school; Aldhelm (d. 709) was the West Saxons' riddler; Bede IV.16 on the tides off the Hamble; Cyneberht bishop of Winchester to 801/3, who went to Rome with Archbishop Aethelheard (Anglo-Saxon Chronicle 799). The infants in the pits and the moved graves: Morton 1992. Willibald's crossing: Huneberc.

pages.game: Eadhun is the pilot at Hamwic, one of the English and a Christian. Found at: the wic-hythe and the boat strand. To look at: about forty, short and thick, skin like a boot, bleached hair, a patched tunic to the knee and bare legs grey with mud, an eel spear over his shoulder and a sounding pole taller than he is.
pages.known: Not in the record: the game's own person, set in a real place. Ead- and -hun are English name parts. The water from a seventeenth-century account quoted by Morton 1992: 13 km of 'good and even soundings', mud flats 'safe for any body to rest on'; the double high water; eel, flounder, bass and mullet, oysters and winkles (Bourdillon and Coy 1980). Beaduheard at Portland, c. 789. The brother is invented; the proverb is turned from a later one (?).

Courteous, slow, and unable to let a far-travelled guest leave without asking him one question. To look at: about sixty-five, tall and stooped, white hair to the shoulder and a white beard, a faded blue wool cloak pinned with an old-fashioned gilt bronze brooch, a horn-handled knife, a bronze dipper in his hand at feasts.
pages.known: Not in the record: the game's own person, set in a real place. Nothing says who owned the Buddha or that anyone knew what it was, and this man does not know either. The guest's fire, water and seat from Hávamál 2-4. Name: Inge- + -mund, both on the Uppland stones.

pages.game: Fastulf is the smith at Helgö, one of the Svear and one who keeps the old gods. Found at: the cold hearths. The last man who lights a hearth in the casters' terraces. Makes kettles whole and pours small lead and bronze weights; proud, exact, and short of metal. To look at: nearly fifty, short and broad, forearms scarred with small burns, grey-brown hair tied back with a thong, a leather apron over a patched tunic, tongs in his belt and a little folding balance in a bronze case round his neck.
pages.known: Not in the record: the game's own person, set in a real place. No smith is named; goldsmiths and bronze-casters from the 400s, the fine casting stopped in the 600s. Rhenish and Mosan brass melted in the north for brooches, and oval brooches cast by the hundred in the towns. Name: Fast- + -ulf.

Ingemund's sister, who keeps the rock, casts the lots and bakes the loaves for the dead. Sharp-eyed, unsentimental, and amused by strangers' gods. To look at: over sixty, small and straight-backed, grey hair in one braid, a brown wool dress and a sheepskin over her shoulders in any weather, a leather bag of cut fruitwood twigs, flour on her hands.
pages.known: Not in the record: the game's own person, set in a real place. Lots cast to learn which god is angry and whether a thing should be done (Rimbert c. 18, 19, 27, 30); offerings at the rock (Zachrisson 2004 (?)); bread in graves (?). The southern sound growing shallower as the land rises. Name: Gud- + -lög (Gudlög, U 328).

pages.known: Not in the record: the game's own person, set in a real place. An ordinary child of the farm, who is how the island remembers the merchant from year to year. Red ground is mould clay, black is the burnt earth of the grave fields. Name: Gil- + -lög (Gillög, U 489).

later.text: Built the castrum (diploma of 2 August 830) and moved the saint, 7-11 June 836 (Ermentarius, Miracula I.1-2).
In 836 Easter fell on 9 April and Pentecost on 28 May, so the seventh of June is the tenth day after it.
Hilbod, abbot from 824/825, still abbot in February 856 (Annals of Angouleme).
